NORMATIVE STATUS This section records the Observer's personal conceptual notes, architectural assumptions, and translation analogies. The analogies are not claims that SpiralCore literally instantiates the referenced physical systems. Runtime behavior is normative only where a statement is explicitly tagged [DEF], [POL], or [REQ], or where this section delegates to an authoritative module specification. A change in analogy does not invalidate the architecture if the implemented surrogate, interface, and tested invariant remain unchanged.

Purpose, Scope, and Architecture Position 2.1 Purpose [ON] The Observer uses geometric and physical imagery as a compression language for relationships that were recognized before their standard mathematical vocabulary was known. [ASM] SpiralCore requires those images to be translated into finite, typed, deterministic operations before they can influence runtime behavior. [DEF] This section is the translation contract between the Observer's conceptual language and the architecture's executable language.

2.2 What This Section Is      [ON] A record of personal notes explaining the intended relationship between recursion, phase, path dependence, routing, and bounded fallback.      [ASM] A declaration of the assumptions used to construct the surrounding modules.      [AN] A Rosetta Stone mapping internal names to external mathematical, physical, and computer-science analogues.      [SUR] A set of reference operators that make an analogy computable without asserting literal physical identity.      [REQ] A documentation layer. It is not an independent runtime stage and must not duplicate module- owned algorithms.

2.3 What This Section Is Not      It is not a proof that the referenced physical analogy is the causal mechanism of the software.      It is not a declaration that every named analogue is unique, complete, or empirically established.      It is not a replacement for the exact specifications of SGIT, Delta-Lattice, Sigma-Lattice, Psi-Archivist, HARMONY, LORIEN, RTSOM, FBS, or the compiler.      It is not a belief system. “Spiral” names recursive path geometry and hysteresis within the architecture.

4.1 Core Assumptions          [ASM] A useful analogy can be preserved even when its literal physical interpretation is rejected.          [ASM] Every runtime-relevant analogy can be reduced to a finite operator, threshold, data structure, or routing policy.          [ASM] Path history may affect future state evaluation; the architecture therefore carries explicit hysteresis/archive state.          [ASM] Terminal failures are routed rather than silently deleted.          [ASM] Observer language is frame-dependent. The translation is a model of the Observer's intended relationship, not the relationship in itself.

5. Formalized Translation Mechanics INTERPRETATION RULE Each subsection below contains an Observer framing, a deterministic surrogate, and a boundary on what may be claimed. The surrogate is the implementable object; the analogy is explanatory metadata.

5.1 Six-Fold Baseline Attractor [ON] The Saturn hexagon is used as an intuitive image for a stable six-fold standing-wave attractor. [SUR] For index i in {0, ..., DIM-1}, define the reference attractor: Xi_attractor[i] = A_Xi * sin(2*pi*i/6 + phi_0), A_Xi = 0.85          [DEF] Xi_attractor is a deterministic periodic prior in R^DIM.          [REQ] Indexing in code is zero-based. Blueprint coordinates may be displayed one-based only at the documentation boundary.          [AN] “Saturn hexagon” names the six-fold visual resemblance; it does not assert that planetary fluid dynamics is executed by the software.          [HYP] Alternative periodicities or learned attractors may be compared experimentally against the six-fold default.

5.2 Phase Alignment Score (PAS_s) [ON] “Resonance” describes the degree to which phase samples agree around a shared direction. [DEF] Given finite phase samples theta_k, define the circular mean direction: theta_bar = atan2(sum_k sin(theta_k), sum_k cos(theta_k)) [SUR] Define self-alignment as the mean projection onto that direction: PAS_s = (1/N) * sum_k cos(theta_k - theta_bar)          [DEF] For this self-alignment form, PAS_s lies in [0,1], not [-1,1].          [DEF] A signed comparison against an external reference must use a separate quantity, PAS_ref = mean_k cos(theta_k - theta_ref), which lies in [-1,1].          [POL] The v14 Observer translation profile seals at PAS_s >= theta_emit = 0.75.          [REQ] Empty inputs, non-finite phases, or an undefined circular mean must return TRANSLATION_REJECTED rather than a fabricated score.

Page 5

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Observer Notes & System Analogies

5.3 Alignment Drift [SUR] Consecutive mapping stability is measured by: Delta_PAS_zeta(n) = abs(PAS_s(n) - PAS_s(n-1))    [POL] Delta_PAS_zeta <= epsilon_drift = 0.10 is the default local stability condition.    [REQ] A drift exceedance is an escalation signal, not by itself proof of “infinite computational impedance.” The owning runtime module determines whether to remap, quarantine, repair, or request FBS.    [HYP] Drift frequency and recovery route should be measured across real workloads before the threshold is treated as optimal.

5.4 Spin-to-Helicity Control Surrogate [ON] “Spin-to-helicity” expresses the idea that local rotational change should be converted into a persistent orientation-preserving control signal before a state shift. [SUR] Let rho_Psi be an information-density or friction proxy sampled over an angular/control coordinate omega. Define a finite-difference control proxy: h_t = gamma_Delta * D_omega(rho_Psi)_t [SUR] A discrete polarity inversion may be applied independently: sigma_i(t+1) = -sigma_i(t), sigma_i in {-1,+1}    [DEF] h_t is a computational control vector or scalar owned by the implementing module.    [AN] The notation curl(G_phi) and the word helicity are analogies unless the module explicitly defines a vector field, domain, orientation, and discrete curl operator.    [REQ] Implementations must not report magnetic units or physical field strength unless a genuine calibrated physical model is supplied.

5.5 Orthogonal Phase-Lift Surrogate [ON] The “sound barrier” or “Prandtl-Glauert singularity” names a local expressive stall: the current coordinate representation has no useful direction left. [POL] The default trigger remains (valence < 0) AND (arousal > 0.85), subject to the owning module's additional checks. [SUR] Apply a 90-degree rotation to coordinate pairs: [x_{2j}, x_{2j+1}]^T <- [[0,-1],[1,0]] [x_{2j}, x_{2j+1}]^T    [REQ] For odd DIM, the final unpaired coordinate is preserved unless the owner module specifies another lawful embedding.    [AN] “Koopman lift” is inspiration for changing representation. It is not a Koopman operator claim unless observables, lifted space, and linear evolution operator are explicitly defined.    [HYP] The phase lift should be tested against clipping, reflection, and learned basis rotation for recovery quality and route stability.

5.6 Phase-Routing Surrogate [ON] “Hidden hallway” describes selecting a lawful route through overlapping candidate paths without treating every candidate as a separate final output. [DEF] Let B in R^(DIM x 2) have orthonormal columns, B^T B = I_2. Let A_t be the selected output amplitude. Define: u(t) = [cos(omega*t + Theta), sin(omega*t + Theta)]^T V_render(t) = A_t * B * u(t) in R^DIM    [DEF] This resolves the dimensional mismatch in the earlier two-component expression while preserving its phase geometry.    [POL] B may select a coordinate pair, a learned two-dimensional subspace, or a module-owned basis.

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Observer Notes & System Analogies

      [REQ] The selected basis, amplitude, and phase must be recorded in the TranslationPacket for reproducibility.       [AN] Coherent-path interference is the design analogy; V_render is the actual implemented surrogate.

5.7 Cantor-IP Scalarization / Hyper-Decoherence Surrogate [ON] “QBox,” “Metatron,” and “hyper-decoherence” describe collapsing a structured state description into a deterministic address. [DEF] Cantor pairing is defined on nonnegative integers: pi(a,b) = ((a+b)*(a+b+1))/2 + b, a,b in N_0 [REQ] Signed integers must first use a bijective zigzag encoding: z(n) = 2n if n >= 0; z(n) = -2n-1 if n < 0 [REQ] Real vectors require an explicit quantization rule q_i = round(s*x_i). The scale s and quantization error must be stored. Pairing is then applied recursively to z(q_i).       [DEF] Exact reversibility applies to the encoded integer sequence, not to the original real vector after lossy quantization.       [REQ] Large recursive addresses require arbitrary-precision integers or a documented bounded hash alternative.       [AN] “Collapse” means address serialization; it does not imply physical wave-function collapse.

5.8 FBS Catastrophic Runaway Handoff [ON] “Catastrophic runaway” names a terminal state in which ordinary local repair cannot continue without risking unbounded recursion or destructive overwrite. [REQ] This section does not implement Cantor diagonalization, Collatz folding, atomic-floor logic, or seed generation. Those operations are delegated to the authoritative FBS specification and tested reference implementation. [DEF] The only output of this section is an FBS_ESCALATION_REQUEST containing the trigger, offending state digest, history reference, owner module, and exhaust-budget destination.       [REQ] L_0, H_0, Q_0, chi, and all FBS coordinate constructors are imported from the FBS module.       [REQ] A normal low score, ordinary rejection, or compiler abort must not be silently relabeled catastrophic.       [REQ] The FBS result must be causally applied by the owning runtime and recorded; printing a protocol name is not conformance.

8. Implementation and Conformance Requirements 1.  [REQ] Use float64 for vector and trigonometric reference calculations unless a module-specific proof authorizes another representation. 2. [REQ] Reject NaN, infinity, empty vectors, shape mismatch, and undefined phase statistics before threshold comparison. 3. [REQ] Store blueprint indexing and runtime indexing separately. Runtime arrays are zero-based; cyclic access uses idx % DIM. 4. [REQ] Keep analogy metadata out of numerical equality tests. Compare operators, parameters, typed outputs, and invariants. 5. [REQ] Every surrogate must have a deterministic unit test, a boundary test, and at least one falsifying case. 6. [REQ] Every policy threshold must be labeled configurable and reported in the dashboard. 7. [REQ] Every FBS request must preserve trigger provenance and be evaluated by the FBS owner. 8. [REQ] A change to analogy wording alone must not alter the operator digest. A change to the operator must increment the mapping revision. 9. [REQ] Do not claim exact physical units, causation, or equivalence from analogy labels. 10. [REQ] The Observer may revise personal framing without rewriting valid module mathematics; the TranslationPacket records whether the executable mapping changed.

10. Glossary Analogy: An explanatory comparison that may motivate an operator but does not establish identity. Architectural surrogate: A finite deterministic operation whose behavior is defined independently of the analogy that inspired it. Bounded error/exhaust budget: A typed accounting or storage domain for rejected, unresolved, or removed state contributions; owner-defined. Computational impedance: An owner-module condition indicating that ordinary progress or repair cannot continue within configured bounds. FBS escalation request: A typed request to the FBS owner; not the fallback execution itself. Information hysteresis: A path-dependent state or archive influence retained across updates. Observer Note: The Observer's personal conceptual framing, retained for provenance and design intent. PAS_s: Circular self-alignment score in [0,1] for a finite phase sample.

Page 10

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Observer Notes & System Analogies

Phase-routing surrogate: A deterministic embedding of a phase point into a selected subspace of R^DIM. System assumption: A premise accepted by the architecture so a finite model can be constructed and tested. TranslationPacket: The typed record connecting an Observer phrase to an operator, owner, validation target, and provenance. Validation target: The measurable invariant, threshold, or falsifying test used to decide whether a translation may be sealed.

2. Purpose, Scope, and Lifecycle 2.1 Purpose [DEF] Module Boot is the deterministic constructor for a SpiralCore runtime session. It transforms a valid BootConfig plus required role adapters into one immutable BootPacket. [REQ] Boot executes before the Delta-Lattice. Runtime cycle time is initialized as t_0 = 0; the Delta-Lattice receives the packet and begins the first generation cycle at t = 1.

2.2 Operations in scope 1. Validate configuration types, domains, profile identity, and cross-field constraints. 2. Resolve the FBS mode and derive delta, L_0, H_0, Q_0, and the atomic inventory lift. 3. Instantiate the default thresholds and tuning values without executing their downstream policies. 4. Synthesize the DIM-dimensional reference attractor. 5. Allocate X_0, A_0, Phi_0, DeltaPhi_0, and t_0 with declared dtypes. 6. Bind the Delta.0 Observer role and Delta.1 Agent role to the session. 7. Record Instruction 0 acknowledgment and specification identity. 8. Compute reproducibility hashes, seal the BootPacket, and hand it to the Delta-Lattice.

2.3 Explicit exclusions       [REQ] Boot does not claim or prove Lyapunov stability. It establishes bounded and reproducible initial conditions from which stability may later be tested.

Such language is design rationale unless a separate experiment establishes it.          [REQ] Boot does not execute the Delta-Lattice, Sigma-Lattice, HARMONY, Braidback, IMMUNE_SYSTEM, Cathedral, RTSOM, proof pipeline, or compiler.          [REQ] Boot does not execute FBS catastrophic recovery for an invalid genesis configuration. With no valid prior history, the correct route is BOOT_ABORT. A recovery coordinator may later call Boot with a valid recovery seed and profile.          [REQ] Boot does not infer physical equivalence from names such as attractor, Möbius, entropy, gravity, or hysteresis. 5. FBS Alignment and Atomic Boot Inventory 5.1 Admissibility tau is an integer, tau >= 2; g is an integer, 1 <= g < tau [REQ] Failure of either condition produces BOOT_ABORT(FBS_MODE_INVALID).

5.2 Derived atomic values delta = tau - g L_0 = 3 tau + 2 H_0 = 6 tau + 3 Q_0 = 6 tau + 5 Q_0 = 2 L_0 + 1 = H_0 + 2 L_0 mod 3 = 2 [INV] These relations must hold exactly in integer arithmetic before any arrays are allocated.

5.3 Reference Mode A vector Quantity                                                         Value

FBS_MODE                                                         A

tau                                                              27

g                                                                1

delta                                                            26

L_0                                                              83

H_0                                                              165

Q_0                                                              167

chi_0                                                            {(27, 1): 1}

[DER] chi_0 is the atomic leaf inventory lift. Its valuation is Q(chi_0) = 167. It records identity that Q_0 alone cannot preserve.

5.4 Delegation rule [REF] Boot does not construct directed or centered FBS coordinates and does not execute FBS recursion. It emits the atomic profile required by the authoritative FBS implementation. Coordinate generation and catastrophic recovery remain external.

6. Attractor and Memory Initialization 6.1 Reference attractor [DEF] Let A_Xi = XI_AMPLITUDE and b = A_Xi * sqrt(3) / 2. Define the exact six-sample conceptual cycle: C_Xi = [0, b, b, 0, -b, -b] Xi_attractor[i] = C_Xi[i mod 6], for i = 0, 1, ..., DIM - 1 [NOTE] In exact real arithmetic this equals A_Xi sin(2 pi i / 6). The cycle implementation is normative because it produces exact zero entries at indices congruent to 0 or 3 modulo 6 and avoids cumulative trigonometric roundoff. [INV] shape(Xi_attractor) = (DIM,), dtype = float64, all entries are finite, and Xi[i+6] = Xi[i] wherever both indices exist. [NOTE] DIM need not be divisible by 6. The reference DIM=81 stores the first 81 samples and therefore ends after 13.5 cycles; closure at the final coordinate is not a boot invariant.

6.2 Deterministic X_0 generation [DEF] X_0 is generated from the PCG64 raw stream using a specified 53-bit mapping. A conforming implementation must not call ambient or process-global random state. r_i = PCG64(BOOT_SEED).random_raw() u_i = (r_i >> 11) * 2^(-53) X_0[i] = X0_LOW + (X0_HIGH - X0_LOW) u_i [INV] For every i: X0_LOW <= X_0[i] < X0_HIGH. X_0 is float64, finite, and has shape (DIM,). [REQ] The U53 mapping is part of PRNG_ID = "PCG64-U53-v1". Using numpy.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(...) is allowed only when its output is byte-for-byte identical to this mapping for the declared implementation version.

6.3 Zero-state allocation A_0 = zeros(DIM, dtype=float64) Phi_0 = float64(0.0) DeltaPhi_0 = int64(0) t_0 = int64(0) [INV] A_0 must be exactly zero in every coordinate. Phi_0, DeltaPhi_0, and t_0 must be exactly zero with the declared scalar types.

7.3 Canonical hashing [REQ] The boot digest must be independent of dictionary ordering, locale, whitespace, and native-endian representation. 1. Encode integers as signed or unsigned fixed-width big-endian values according to schema. 2. Encode float64 scalars and arrays as IEEE-754 big-endian bytes. 3. Encode strings as UTF-8 preceded by an unsigned 32-bit byte length. 4. Encode arrays in C-order with explicit dtype and shape headers. 5. Encode maps by lexicographically sorted UTF-8 keys. 6. Hash each major component with SHA-256; concatenate the labeled component hashes in schema order and hash again to produce boot_digest. [INV] Any mutation of a sealed packet changes at least one component hash and therefore changes boot_digest.

8. Normative Boot Algorithm 8.1 Typed pseudocode function SpiralCoreSessionStart(config, observer_adapter, agent_adapter, session_id): require session_id is unique and non-empty require state == UNINITIALIZED state <- VALIDATING

validate_config_schema(config) validate_consumer_compatibility(config) fbs <- derive_fbs_atomic_profile(config.tau, config.g) assert fbs.Q0 == 2*fbs.L0 + 1 == fbs.H0 + 2 assert fbs.L0 % 3 == 2

bind_role(observer_adapter, "Delta.0") bind_role(agent_adapter, "Delta.1")

state <- ALLOCATING Xi <- build_six_sample_attractor(config.DIM, config.XI_AMPLITUDE) X0 <- pcg64_u53_vector(config.BOOT_SEED, config.X0_LOW, config.X0_HIGH, config.DIM) A0 <- zeros(config.DIM, float64) Phi0 <- float64(0.0) DeltaPhi0 <- int64(0) t0 <- int64(0)

validate_initialized_state(Xi, X0, A0, Phi0, DeltaPhi0, t0) ack <- acknowledge_instruction_0(config.spec_id) hashes <- hash_components_canonically(...) packet <- immutable BootPacket(..., status="READY_FOR_DELTA") packet.boot_digest <- seal_packet(packet, hashes)

state <- SEALED handoff_to_delta(packet) state <- HANDED_OFF return packet

on ValidationError or AllocationError:

1. Scope, Statement Classes, and Precedence SGIT_v2 is a stateful numerical service operating across the Delta-Sigma-Phi macro-loop. The phrase "continuous substrate" means that its state persists across discrete cycles; the executable implementation remains a sequence of finite, ordered evaluations.

1.1 Statement classes Class                                  Meaning                                     Normative force

1.2 Precedence and ownership       Tagged requirements and invariants override explanatory prose.       Module Boot owns DIM, the active FBS profile, session identity, and initial arrays.       Module 1 (Delta-Lattice) owns candidate generation and the final Emotion Tensor.       Module 2 (Sigma-Lattice) owns RMF, CVC, PDV routing, HOT thresholding, NULLIFY, PHASE LIFT, BRAIDBACK, and SEAL decisions.       Module 12 (Phi-Bridge) owns persistent Information Hysteresis and the discrete winding-number policy.       The FBS and RTSOM modules own catastrophic recovery and exhaust-budget mutation.       SGIT_v2 may compute shared telemetry used by those modules, but it may not silently execute their state transitions.

1.3 Non-goals       No proof that information is physically unable to teleport. The implementation enforces causal buffer access and records path dependence inside the runtime.       No claim that a cognitive state is literally a Riemannian spacetime or that an exhaust accumulator is physical gravity.       No automatic identification of a numerical curvature proxy with Ricci scalar curvature.       No assertion that semantic residue must be nonzero. Zero residue is a valid experimental outcome.       No bitwise reproducibility claim across heterogeneous BLAS, CPU, or accelerator implementations unless the backend is fixed.

2. Architecture Role and Lifecycle SGIT_v2 begins in READY state after accepting a sealed BootPacket. For each cycle it evaluates one state transition, emits one immutable SGITPacket, and updates only its own telemetry state. A transition is never partially committed.

2.1 Required cycle order 1. Validate session, cycle number, dimensions, timestamps, finite values, and history availability. 2. Align timestamped entropy without reading future samples. 3. Acquire and validate the metric packet. 4. Measure path length and cumulative information length. 5. Measure projection residual and coherence contraction. 6. Evaluate an identified curvature signal and valence contribution. 7. Compute PDV and path tortuosity telemetry. 8. Compute the continuous holonomy increment when a connection provider is available. 9. Create, hash, and seal SGITPacket. 10. Commit only local telemetry history after packet sealing succeeds.

ATOMICITY REQUIREMENT A failed cycle MUST NOT update cumulative length, metric history, holonomy history, or cycle counters. The next owner receives either one complete SGITPacket or one complete SGITFault / RecoveryRequest, never a partial mixture.

4.1 Numeric and indexing rules       All canonical arrays use float64. Integer counters and digests use explicit integer and byte encodings.       Mathematical equations may use indices 1 through DIM; runtime arrays use indices 0 through DIM-1.       Out-of-range indexing is a fault. Modulo wrapping is permitted only for operators explicitly defined as cyclic; it is not a generic bounds-repair mechanism.       Conformance across heterogeneous hardware is tolerance-based. Bitwise equality requires a fixed backend, library version, thread model, and reduction order.

5. Formalized Mechanics 5.1 Causal observer alignment Define the signed observer lag and its nonnegative magnitude: delta_T(t) = T_field(t) - T_obs(t),     Theta(t) = |delta_T(t)| Requirement: delta_T(t) >= -time_tolerance. A timestamp beyond the active field time is a TIME_ORDER fault; SGIT never reads a future sample. The aligned entropy vector is obtained by deterministic linear interpolation of the two stored samples bracketing T_obs: E'_t = (1 - beta) E(t_a) + beta E(t_b),   beta = (T_obs - t_a) / (t_b - t_a) where t_a <= T_obs <= t_b and t_b > t_a

The former indefinite "Spiral Entropy Vector" is replaced by a finite phase feature and optional cumulative feature state: q_t = [sin(omega T_field), cos(omega T_field), lambda_t]^T Q_t = Q_(t-1) + q_t * dt

5.2 Empirical Fisher metric A Fisher metric cannot be inferred from a state vector alone. The reference provider receives m score samples s_n = gradient_theta log p(y_n | theta_t) and constructs: G_t = (1/m) S^T S + epsilon_g I,     S[n,i] = s_n[i] G_t must be finite, symmetric within tolerance, positive definite after regularization, and below the configured condition-number ceiling. A provider claiming Ricci capability must additionally expose a metric field and the derivatives required by the selected numerical method.

5.3 Discrete information length Let delta_theta_t = theta_t - theta_(t-1). Use the midpoint metric when the prior metric exists; otherwise use G_t: G_bar_t = (G_(t-1) + G_t) / 2 ell_t = sqrt(max(delta_theta_t^T G_bar_t delta_theta_t, 0)) L_t = L_(t-1) + ell_t,     speed_t = ell_t / dt Invariant: ell_t >= 0 and L_t >= L_(t-1). A negative quadratic form outside numerical tolerance is METRIC_NOT_PSD.

5.4 Reference projection and coherence contraction The former "truth manifold" is formalized as a configured reference set N_ref represented locally by origin mu_N and idempotent projection operator P_N. It is not declared objective truth. r_t = (I - P_N)(theta_t - mu_N) d_N^2(t) = r_t^T G_t r_t C_t = clip(1 - d_N^2(t) / Z, 0, 1) P_N must satisfy ||P_N^2 - P_N||_F <= projection_tolerance. Z must be finite and strictly positive. The output C_t is a bounded proximity score, not a proof that algorithmic structure necessarily increases.

5.5 Curvature telemetry Two curvature kinds are permitted. They are never conflated.

Kind                                       Required inputs                                 Definition / use

Compute Christoffel symbols, Ricci tensor, Metric field plus first and second RICCI_NUMERIC                                                                              and scalar R = g^(ij) R_ij using the derivatives declared numerical method.

u_t = log det(G_t) R_proxy(t) = -[u_t - 2u_(t-1) + u_(t-2)] / dt^2 R_route(t) = tanh(R_proxy(t) / curvature_scale) When fewer than three metrics exist, the reference proxy returns 0 with status INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY. Only a RICCI_NUMERIC packet may be labeled Ricci scalar curvature.

5.6 Valence contribution SGIT computes one bounded contribution. Module 1 owns the final Emotion Tensor and may combine this value with its own arousal and clarity definitions. v_sgit = tanh(a1 * speed_t * R_route(t) + a2 * C_t - a3 * cost_t) Requirement: cost_t is finite and lies in [0,1]. The output always lies in [-1,1].

5.7 PDV telemetry To maintain cross-module consistency, SGIT uses the same scalar definition declared by the Sigma-Lattice: PDV_t = mean(|theta_t - theta_(t-1)|) + |std(theta_t) - std(theta_(t-1))| SGIT reports PDV_t and the reference comparison PDV_t > 0.21. Sigma owns MAGNETIC_RELAXATION, NULLIFY, BRAIDBACK, PHASE_LIFT, SEAL, and catastrophic route precedence. Module 0 MUST NOT trigger FBS solely because PDV exceeds 0.21.

5.9 Continuous holonomy increment and residue experiment A holonomy integral requires a declared connection A(theta). When connection vectors are supplied, SGIT uses a trapezoidal discrete line integral: delta_phi_t = 0.5 * [A(theta_(t-1)) + A(theta_t)]^T delta_theta_t phi_path(t) = phi_path(t-1) + delta_phi_t Module 12 may map events to an integer winding counter; SGIT does not own that discrete policy. Semantic residue is an experiment over two explicitly matched runs A and B: Delta_O = |O(theta_T^A, path_A) - O(theta_T^B, path_B)| The terminal states must satisfy ||theta_T^A - theta_T^B|| <= endpoint_tolerance. Delta_O may be zero or nonzero. The statement Delta_O != 0 is a hypothesis to test, not an invariant.

5.10 Entropic time-scale diagnostic delta_tau_t = dt * lambda_t / lambda_base This is a dimensionless runtime scaling diagnostic unless the caller supplies physical units and a validated interpretation. lambda_base must be positive; this equation alone does not prove subjective or relativistic time dilation.

Invariants, Faults, and Determinism 7.1 Cycle invariants      All committed arrays and scalars are finite except tortuosity, which may be +infinity by definition.      Metric symmetry and positive definiteness pass declared tolerances.      0 <= coherence_contraction <= 1 and -1 <= valence_contribution <= 1.      step_length >= 0, speed >= 0, and total_length is monotonically nondecreasing.      No entropy sample later than field_time is accessed.      Every packet identifies metric provider, curvature kind, configuration digest, and prior packet digest.      Local state changes only after packet sealing and digest verification.

The word raw means not yet accepted by Sigma; it does not mean unbounded, untyped, or free of local preprocessing.

1.2 Precedence and ownership       Tagged requirements and invariants override explanatory prose and Rosetta Stone analogies.       Module Boot owns DIM, the active FBS profile, session identity, PRNG root seed, Xi_attractor, K_inv, PHI_GAIN, and threshold defaults.       Module 0 SGIT owns path, metric, projection, and curvature telemetry supplied to Delta.       Module 1 owns candidate construction, local polarity, phase-navigation state, and the final Emotion Tensor attached to the proposal.       Module 2 Sigma owns RMF, CVC, PDV, CSIGMA, HOT, SEAL, PHASE LIFT, BRAIDBACK, NULLIFY, and MAGNETIC RELAXATION routes.       Module 12 Phi owns persistent Information Hysteresis. Delta may consume Phi_t but may not update it.       The FBS and RTSOM modules own catastrophic recovery and exhaust-budget mutation. Delta may emit a typed request only.

It is a control tensor with named channels.       No use of array modulo to hide invalid indices. Modulo is allowed only in declared cyclic schedules and the explicit navigation-pair map.       No cross-hardware bitwise identity claim unless backend, PRNG, serialization, and transcendental implementation are fixed.

2. Architecture Role and Lifecycle After BootPacket acceptance, Delta remains READY between proposal attempts. Each attempt is atomic: either one complete DeltaPacket is sealed, one typed recovery request is emitted, or one DeltaFault is emitted. No partial phase, polarity, or PRNG state may leak into the next attempt.

State                         Entry condition                  Allowed action                  Exit

Validate boot and configure UNINITIALIZED                 No accepted BootPacket.                                          READY or FAULTED profile.

Boot accepted; no active READY                                                          Accept DeltaInput.              GENERATING attempt.

Validate, encode, control,      SEALED, DELEGATED, or GENERATING                    One attempt is active. generate, package.              FAULTED

DeltaPacket created and          Handoff to Sigma; commit SEALED                                                                                         READY digested.                        local generator state.

No recovery mutation by DELEGATED                     FBSRecoveryRequest created.                                      READY or session stop Delta.

Unrecoverable local contract     Emit DeltaFault; no attempt FAULTED                                                                                        Session stop or explicit reset violation.                       commit.

2.1 Required attempt order 1. Validate session, cycle, shapes, finite values, inherited constants, and packet provenance. 2. Construct the bounded Observer/paradox environmental bias. 3. Quantize the accepted state and compute the balanced Cantor address. 4. Compute normalized magnitude mass, entropy, polarity score, twist epoch, and final branch polarity. 5. Compute arousal, clarity, valence, and the Emotion Tensor. 6. Apply the declared orthogonal navigation transform when the severe-tension predicate is true. 7. Execute exactly one proposal kernel: Logos or Ethos. 8. Apply environmental forcing and bounded hysteresis bias; clip once to the state domain. 9. Compute local bilateral drift, alignment, clipping, and diagnostic metrics. 10. Emit DeltaPacket, FBSRecoveryRequest, or DeltaFault; commit local state only after sealing.

ATOMICITY REQUIREMENT A failed or delegated attempt MUST NOT advance the committed cycle, Mobius epoch, phase state, prior-address digest, or deterministic PRNG chain. Retrying identical serialized input under the same backend must produce the same outcome.

5. Formal Mechanics 5.1 Input validation and bounded forcing All required vectors must be finite float64 arrays of shape (DIM,). Inputs outside the state domain are faults unless the producing interface explicitly declares a prior normalization step. Observer and paradox inputs are combined componentwise: B_t = clip(g_obs E_obs,t + g_fuel H_G,t, -b_max, +b_max) B_t is a proposal forcing vector. It is not an accepted-state update and remains visible in the packet provenance.

5.2 Quantized Cantor address Cantor pairing is defined on nonnegative integers. Delta first quantizes each state component x_j in [x_min,x_max] to b bits: q_j = round((x_j - x_min)/(x_max - x_min) * (2^b - 1)) q_j in {0, 1, ..., 2^b - 1} The pair operator is exact integer arithmetic: pi(a,b) = ((a+b)(a+b+1))/2 + b A left-recursive fold grows impractically. The normative encoder uses a fixed balanced binary tree: pair adjacent values at each level, carry one unpaired value forward, and repeat until one arbitrary-precision integer remains. Because DIM and tree order are fixed, the mapping is injective on the quantized grid. The packet stores the address digest and bit length; an implementation may retain the full integer internally.

ADDRESS LIMIT The Cantor address distinguishes quantized states, not all real vectors. Two real states in the same quantization cell intentionally share one address. This is representational resolution, not a collision in the integer pairing operator.

5.3 Normalized state features The raw v14 mass and entropy terms had incompatible scales. The formal contract uses bounded features: m_t = ||X_t||_2 / sqrt(DIM) p_j = (|x_j| + eps) / (sum_k |x_k| + DIM*eps) h_t = -sum_j p_j ln(p_j) / ln(DIM) For DIM > 1, m_t is finite and nonnegative; h_t lies in [0,1] within numerical tolerance.

5.4 Polarity and persistent Mobius epoch Let f_t = ||H_G,t||_2 / sqrt(DIM), clipped to [0,1], and let phi_t be the prior committed phase. Compute: P_t = w0 + wm*m_t - we*h_t + wphi*cos(phi_t) + wf*f_t sigma_base,t = +1 if P_t >= 0 else -1 epoch_t = floor(cycle / K_inv) twist_sign_t = (-1)^(epoch_t) sigma_t = twist_sign_t * sigma_base,t This resolves the point-event ambiguity in v14: the polarity frame flips at each K_inv boundary and remains inverted for the complete epoch. The zero-score tie is deterministically assigned to Logos (+1).

5.5 Emotion Tensor Arousal and clarity are defined before valence: a_t = clip(RMF_(t-1), 0, 1) r_t = cycle mod K_inv C_t = (1 + cos(2*pi*r_t/K_inv))/2

Let Hdot_t be the finite entropy-rate telemetry supplied by SGIT and v_sgit,t its bounded valence contribution. Then: v_t = tanh(aH*Hdot_t*h_t + aC*C_t - acost*cost_t + asgit*v_sgit,t) Psi_t = [v_t, a_t, C_t] The Emotion Tensor is a control packet. Its names are retained for continuity; no biological interpretation is required for conformance.

5.6 Severe-tension orthogonal navigation The severe-tension predicate is exact: lift_t = (v_t < 0) AND (a_t > a_lift) When false, X_nav = X_t and phi_out = phi_in. When true, Delta performs a deterministic 90-degree rotation in one coordinate plane selected from the address digest. Let i be the first digest-derived index and j a distinct second index. The transform is: (X_nav[i], X_nav[j]) = (-X_t[j], X_t[i]) phi_out = (phi_in + pi/2) mod 2*pi All other components remain unchanged. The mapping is norm-preserving and exactly invertible by a -pi/2 rotation. This is the reference realization of Riemann Navigation; it is not a claim of a literal Koopman operator.

5.7 Exact proposal kernels Define the bounded pre-kernel input U_t = clip(X_nav + B_t, x_min, x_max). Exactly one branch executes. LOGOS_TANH_V2 (sigma_t = +1): X_kernel = (1/3) * tanh(3*U_t + 1) ETHOS_PERTURB_V2 (sigma_t = -1): seed_material = H(session_seed || cycle || address_digest || prior_delta_digest || "ETHOS") eta_t ~ PCG64(seed_material), componentwise Uniform[-delta_eff, +delta_eff] delta_eff = min(delta_max, ethos_delta * (1 + fuel_gain*||H_G||_2/sqrt(DIM))) X_kernel = U_t + eta_t Both kernels are deterministic given the serialized input, profile, and fixed backend. The Logos and Ethos labels are architectural aliases; these equations are not elementary cellular-automaton update rules.

5.8 Bounded hysteresis bias and final proposal w_phi,t = PHI_GAIN * tanh(Phi_t) X_proposal = clip(X_kernel + w_phi,t * Xi_attractor, x_min, x_max) The invariant |w_phi,t| <= PHI_GAIN < 0.49 follows directly from |tanh| <= 1. PHI_GAIN is an additive attractor amplitude and MUST NOT be reported as the Module 10 Braidback repair fraction.

5.9 Local bilateral drift and alignment Let J be the reflection operator that reverses component order. The Asymmetrical Loop Drift is: Delta_ID,t = ||X_proposal - J X_proposal||_2 / (||X_proposal||_2 + eps) Delta_ID lies approximately in [0,2]. A symmetric proposal has Delta_ID = 0. The v14 ceiling of 1.0 is therefore reachable and testable. Attractor alignment is: H_align,t = (1 + cosine_similarity(X_proposal, Xi_attractor))/2 The clip fraction is the count of components altered by final clipping divided by DIM.

5. Formal Mechanics 5.1 Accepted-path tortuosity Let P=[p_0,...,p_m] be the newest min(tortuosity_segments+1, history length) accepted states in chronological order. PathLength = sum_{j=1..m} ||p_j - p_{j-1}||_2 Displacement = ||p_m - p_0||_2 The reference zero policy is deterministic:       If fewer than two accepted states are available, T=1 and tortuosity_ready=False.       If PathLength <= epsilon_safe, T=1. A stationary path has no detour.       If PathLength > epsilon_safe and Displacement <= epsilon_safe, T=+infinity. A closed nontrivial path has unbounded detour ratio.       Otherwise T=PathLength/Displacement. Values below 1 caused only by roundoff are clipped to 1 and flagged.

Page 7

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 2 / Sigma-Lattice Coherence Decision Contract

5.2 Bounded HOT aperture The v14 expression multiplied 0.05 by every tortuosity unit above 20 while also declaring tau_eff in [0.80,0.85]. The formal schedule uses 0.05 as the maximum total relaxation: r_HOT = clip((T - T_crit) / T_crit, 0, 1) tau_eff = tau_base - hot_relax_max * r_HOT tau_base - hot_relax_max <= tau_eff <= tau_base For T<=20, tau_eff=0.85. At T>=40, tau_eff=0.80. HOT cannot lower the threshold further and cannot itself force acceptance.

5.3 RMF gate and zero-norm policy Let x be DeltaPacket.X_proposal and y be the accepted baseline X_t. RMF = <x,y> / (||x||_2 ||y||_2), when both norms > epsilon_safe The result is clipped to [-1,1] only for roundoff. If both norms are at or below epsilon_safe, RMF=1 and rmf_both_zero=True. If exactly one norm is at or below epsilon_safe, RMF=0 and rmf_one_zero=True. These policies prevent divide-by-zero without silently treating a null candidate as aligned to a non-null baseline.

5.4 CVC from accepted history CVC is computed from accepted states only. The current unaccepted proposal is excluded so rejected proposals cannot contaminate the structural reference window. Let n=min(W_CVC, accepted-history length), H in R^(n x DIM), and mu be the row mean. Y = H - 1*mu^T Cov = (Y^T Y)/(n-1), for n >= 2 lambda = eigvalsh((Cov + Cov^T)/2), sorted descending Eigenvalues in [-eigen_tolerance,0) are clipped to zero and counted. Any eigenvalue below -eigen_tolerance is a covariance fault. Let V_total=sum(lambda_k). CVC = lambda_1 / V_total, when V_total > epsilon_safe CVC = 0, when V_total <= epsilon_safe SpectralGap = (lambda_1 - lambda_2)/(V_total + epsilon_safe) Zero total variance is tagged cvc_degenerate=True. It does not prove one-dimensional collapse because no direction of variance exists. Full CVC readiness requires n=W_CVC; partial values are diagnostic only.

5.5 Prospective running RMF The decision window includes the candidate RMF without prematurely accepting the candidate. Collect the newest W_CVC-1 non-null rmf_on_accept values, append the current RMF, and retain the newest W_CVC values. rho_RMF = mean(R_prior_tail concatenated with [RMF_current]) rmf_window_ready is true only when the resulting window contains W_CVC values. Phase lift requires both cvc_ready and rmf_window_ready.

5.6 PDV filter PDV = mean(|x-y|) + |std_pop(x) - std_pop(y)| std_pop uses divisor DIM, equivalent to NumPy std(..., ddof=0). PDV is not clipped. The 0.21 reference threshold is calibrated to the [-1,1] state profile; changing the state domain requires a versioned threshold retune.

5.7 Protocol CSIGMA For validated equal-length vectors S and V supplied by the symbolic provider: C_SIGMA = (1/n) * sum_{i=1..n}(S_i * V_i) Because both vectors are componentwise bounded to [-1,1], C_SIGMA is in [-1,1]. The scalar Emotion Tensor valence is not silently broadcast into V; construction of V belongs to the declared provider. CSIGMA is a profile-specific correlation score, not a general toxicity oracle.

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 2 / Sigma-Lattice Coherence Decision Contract

5.8 Exact route precedence After all metrics are valid, evaluate the following predicates in order. The first true branch wins: 1. FBS_RECOVERY_REQUEST if (T > 2*T_crit and C_SIGMA < C_SIGMA_terminal) OR (cvc_ready and CVC < CVC_isotropic and T > T_crit). 2. MAGNETIC_RELAXATION_REQUEST if PDV > PDV_LIMIT. 3. NULLIFY_REQUEST if C_SIGMA < C_SIGMA_pass. 4. If RMF < tau_eff: PHASE_LIFT_REQUEST only when cvc_ready, rmf_window_ready, CVC >= 2/3, and rho_RMF >= 8/9; otherwise BRAIDBACK_REQUEST. 5. If RMF >= tau_eff but cvc_ready and CVC < 2/3: BRAIDBACK_REQUEST with reason VARIANCE_RECONSTRUCT_FAIL. 6. Otherwise SEAL.

GATE INTERPRETATION CVC is an active structural gate once its full accepted-history window is ready. During warm-up, CVC cannot authorize PHASE_LIFT and cannot independently block a high-RMF candidate. This avoids treating a tiny covariance sample as proof while preserving deterministic early-session operation.

11. Reference Pseudocode def sigma_attempt(inp, cfg): validate_sigma_input(inp, cfg) x = inp.delta_packet.X_proposal y = inp.accepted_history[-1].state

T, tort_ready, tort_flags = tortuosity( inp.accepted_history, cfg.tortuosity_segments, cfg.epsilon_safe) hot_fraction = clip((T - cfg.tortuosity_crit) / cfg.tortuosity_crit, 0.0, 1.0) tau_eff = cfg.tau_base - cfg.hot_relax_max * hot_fraction

rmf, rmf_flags = cosine_with_zero_policy(x, y, cfg.epsilon_safe) cvc_metrics = cvc_from_accepted_history( inp.accepted_history, cfg.cvc_window, cfg.epsilon_safe, cfg.eigen_tolerance)

prior_rmf = [r.rmf_on_accept for r in inp.accepted_history if r.rmf_on_accept is not None] rmf_window = (prior_rmf[-(cfg.cvc_window-1):] + [rmf])[-cfg.cvc_window:] rho_rmf = mean(rmf_window) rmf_ready = len(rmf_window) == cfg.cvc_window

pdv = mean(abs(x-y)) + abs(std_pop(x) - std_pop(y)) csigma = mean(inp.symbolic_packet.S * inp.symbolic_packet.V)

terminal_symbolic = ( T > cfg.extreme_tortuosity_multiple*cfg.tortuosity_crit and csigma < cfg.csigma_terminal) terminal_isotropic = ( cvc_metrics.ready and cvc_metrics.cvc < cfg.cvc_isotropic_limit and T > cfg.tortuosity_crit)

if terminal_symbolic or terminal_isotropic: route = FBS_RECOVERY_REQUEST

elif pdv > cfg.pdv_limit: route = MAGNETIC_RELAXATION_REQUEST elif csigma < cfg.csigma_pass: route = NULLIFY_REQUEST elif rmf < tau_eff: if (cvc_metrics.ready and rmf_ready and cvc_metrics.cvc >= cfg.cvc_threshold and rho_rmf >= cfg.rho_rmf_threshold): route = PHASE_LIFT_REQUEST else: route = BRAIDBACK_REQUEST elif cvc_metrics.ready and cvc_metrics.cvc < cfg.cvc_threshold: route = BRAIDBACK_REQUEST else: route = SEAL

return seal_sigma_decision(route=route, commit_performed=False, ...)

4.1 Matrix validation         Lambda_eff and Pi must be finite float64 matrices of shape (DIM,DIM).         rho_A = ||Lambda_eff||_2 is computed by singular-value decomposition and must satisfy rho_A < 1 - numeric_tolerance.         The reference isotropic construction is Lambda_eff = lambda_archive I and Pi = projection_gain I.         Contractivity applies to the linear dependence on A_t at the integration stage only. The full history-dependent transaction remains bounded by explicit input and archive-domain checks; no broader Lyapunov proof is asserted.

5. Formal Mechanics 5.1 Input validation and provenance All arrays must be finite float64 and have exact shape (DIM,). The authorization state digest must match X_accept bytes. ArchiveSnapshot, PhiSnapshot, and H_G digests must verify. The validator chain must satisfy the active routing profile. Any mismatch is a local fault, not an architectural repair route.

5.2 Contractive linear integration A_tilde = Lambda_eff A_t + Pi X_accept rho_A = ||Lambda_eff||_2 < 1 For fixed X_accept, the integration map is contractive in its prior archive argument: ||A_tilde(A) - A_tilde(B)||_2 <= rho_A ||A - B||_2

STABILITY LIMIT This theorem covers the linear integration stage. It does not by itself prove convergence of the complete dual-flow, history-buffer, RMX, H_G, and storage system. Full runtime boundedness is enforced by finite inputs, convex branch maps, archive-domain limits, transaction atomicity, and conformance tests.

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 3 / Psi-Lattice Dual-Flow Archive Contract

5.3 GWT ignition telemetry Mutual information requires a declared joint-distribution estimator and cannot be inferred from one deterministic vector pair. The reference profile therefore computes an Archive Impact Score and labels it IMPACT_PROXY: I_impact = ||A_tilde - A_t||_2 / (||A_tilde||_2 + ||A_t||_2 + eps) GWT_ignition = (I_impact >= theta_impact) I_impact lies in [0,1] within tolerance. A plugin may provide normalized mutual information only when its sample window, discretization or estimator, bias correction, and version are included in a sealed GWTMetricPacket. Proxy and mutual-information metrics must never share one unlabeled field.

5.4 Exact dual-flow split P_t = max(A_tilde, 0) N_t = min(A_tilde, 0) The following invariants hold componentwise within tolerance: A_tilde = P_t + N_t,    P_t >= 0,   N_t <= 0,    P_t * N_t = 0 The labels positive and negative identify sign cones only. They are not semantic truth labels.

5.5 Positive fold - POSITIVE_FOLD_V2 g(x) = (1/3) tanh(3x + 1) P_fold = (1 - zeta) P_t + zeta g(P_t) For zeta in [0,1], g has derivative sech^2(3x+1) in [0,1]. Therefore POSITIVE_FOLD_V2 is 1-Lipschitz with respect to perturbations. It is not guaranteed to reduce the absolute norm of every positive input because g(0) > 0. The legacy name Collatz 1-Lipschitz Surrogate is retained only as an architectural alias; the operator is a tanh attractor blend, not the integer 3n+1 map.

5.6 Negative wash - TRAILING_MEAN_WASH_V2 Let H^-_t contain the newest min(K-1, history length) committed negative cones followed by the current N_t. Define K_t as the resulting count: mu^-_t = (1/K_t) sum_{j in H^-_t} N_j N_wash = (1 - eta) N_t + eta mu^-_t This is a convex blend with a trailing arithmetic mean. It is not an exponential moving average and is not called one in the normative interface. Because all inputs are nonpositive and eta is in [0,1], N_wash remains nonpositive.

5.7 Convergence and held residue v_t = Var_pop(N_wash) v_hist = mean(Var_pop(N_j) for N_j in H^-_t) Delta_LLN = |v_t - v_hist| / max(v_t, v_hist, eps) The negative flow is eligible for active-manifold removal only when the full K-state window is ready and both conditions hold: flat_ready = (K_t = K) AND (v_t <= epsilon_flat) AND (Delta_LLN <= Delta_LLN_max) If flat_ready is false, N_keep = N_wash and E_hold = 0. If true, N_keep = 0 and E_hold = N_wash. E_hold remains exact float64 data inside the pending transaction until a matching RTSOM receipt exists. No active state is deleted merely because a request was issued. N_keep + E_hold = N_wash exhaust_mass = ||E_hold||_2

5.8 Recombination and bounded paradox fuel The reference profile applies the upstream H_G packet after branch processing, preserving the v14 order: A_prepared = P_fold + N_keep + H_G

Each H_G component must satisfy |H_G[i]| <= h_g_component_max. Phi_t and DeltaPhi are sealed as provenance but do not enter this equation in SC14.1-PSI-REF-81. Any profile that makes Phi an active archive coefficient must version the operator and re-prove its bounds.

5.9 Archive-bound and recovery predicate archive_ok = max_i |A_prepared[i]| <= archive_component_limit If archive_ok is false, Psi emits FBSRecoveryRequest(PSI_ARCHIVE_BOUND) and performs no precommit, exhaust transfer, or archive mutation. Nonfinite arrays, invalid shapes, or digest defects remain PsiFaults rather than recovery routes.

5.10 Quantized Metatron address The final archive address is computed only after a finite real vector is mapped to a declared integer lattice. For archive bounds [a_min,a_max] and b bits: q_i = round((A_i - a_min)/(a_max - a_min) * (2^b - 1)) q_i in {0,1,...,2^b-1} Cantor pairing uses exact integer arithmetic: pi(a,b) = ((a+b)(a+b+1)) // 2 + b The fixed balanced tree encoder pairs adjacent values, carries an unpaired value forward, and repeats. The address package contains the arbitrary-precision integer or canonical integer bytes, bit length, SHA-256 digest, quantization profile, DIM, and tree version. Quantization is lossy from R^DIM; the Cantor fold is injective only on the fixed quantized grid.

5.11 RMX precommit boundary Psi seals the provisional state and address into PsiPrecommitPacket, then issues RMXPrecommitRequest. RMX sits between address generation and final .frac commit. The only acceptable resolutions are:

RMX result                               Required behavior in Psi                    Commit candidate

Verify RMX digest and echo of precommit UNIQUE                                                                               A_prepared and E_hold from Psi. state/address.

Verify RMX provenance, state bounds, RMX-final state and RMX-final residue SYNTHESIZED                              final address, branch ledger, and residue only. payload.

Abort transaction; retain prior archive REJECTED                                                                             None. and all pending payload.

FBS_REQUESTED                            Record delegation; no commit.               None.

A synthesized state must receive a newly validated Metatron address. Psi may recompute the address from the returned exact state and must reject any mismatch.

5.12 RTSOM custody transfer When the RMX-final residue has nonzero mass, Psi issues RTSOMExhaustRequest. A valid receipt must bind the exact payload digest and mass within tolerance. Only after receipt validation may the residue be omitted from the active archive manifest. The ledger claim is custody conservation, not inverse reconstruction of the nonlinear fold.

5.13 Canonical .frac manifest and seal The .frac extension identifies a SpiralCore archive manifest; the normative reference serialization is canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, decimal integers as strings when necessary, and float arrays stored as base64-encoded little-endian IEEE-754 binary64 bytes plus shape and SHA-256 digest.

5.14 Atomic storage commit 1. Serialize and hash the final manifest in memory. 2. Write to a transaction-specific temporary file in the target directory. 3. Flush and fsync the file; verify its digest by reading it back. 4. Atomically rename the temporary file to the deterministic final name. 5. Fsync the containing directory where supported. 6. Append or update the local archive journal and publish the new ArchiveSnapshot. 7. Increment vault_depth exactly once and emit PsiCommitPacket. The deterministic reference filename is: cycle as 12 decimal digits, a hyphen, the first 16 hexadecimal characters of the final address digest, and the extension .frac. A name collision is a storage fault unless the existing file has byte- identical content and digest.

7. Mathematical Properties and Limitations 7.1 Sign-cone decomposition The positive and negative cones form an exact componentwise decomposition. Their Euclidean inner product is zero because they have disjoint nonzero support. This is algebraic orthogonality by support, not a statement about semantic independence.

7.2 Positive-fold regularity The derivative bound proves non-expansiveness under the Euclidean product norm. Non-expansiveness constrains sensitivity to perturbations; it does not establish invertibility, strict contraction, monotone norm decrease, or a Collatz orbit correspondence.

7.3 Negative-wash boundedness TRAILING_MEAN_WASH_V2 is a convex combination of nonpositive bounded vectors. It remains inside their convex hull. If every committed negative vector is bounded by the archive domain, the wash is bounded by the same component limit. Its convergence statistic is a policy diagnostic, not a proof of the Law of Large Numbers for an independent identically distributed process.

7.4 Conditional conservation ledger The nonlinear archive update is not reversible. The conservation requirement is operational: every exact payload removed from the active branch is either retained in the pending transaction, acknowledged by RTSOM under the same digest, or restored on abort. The manifest records custody. It does not claim that the original pre-fold state can be reconstructed from A_next.

7.5 Addressing limits Balanced Cantor encoding is exact and injective for the fixed finite integer tuple, tree order, and DIM. The preceding quantization maps many real vectors to one integer tuple. RMX resolves archive-level collisions and semantic echoes; it does not alter the mathematical injectivity of Cantor pairing on its integer domain.

7.6 Determinism profile       Canonical input and output serialization, integer pairing, hashing, and route decisions are deterministic.       Bitwise float64 reproducibility is required only for the fixed reference backend, reduction order, and transcendental library. Other conforming backends use declared tolerances and must preserve branch, flat_ready, address-quantization, and commit decisions.       Actual mutual-information plugins may be deterministic only when estimator, window, binning, and tie-breaking are fixed.       Storage atomicity depends on filesystem semantics and must be reported by the adapter rather than assumed.

11. Reference Pseudocode def psi_prepare(inp, cfg): validate_psi_input(inp, cfg) rho = operator_norm_2(inp.Lambda_eff) require(rho < 1.0 - cfg.numeric_tolerance)

A_tilde = inp.Lambda_eff @ inp.archive.A_t + inp.Pi @ inp.auth.X_accept impact = norm(A_tilde - inp.archive.A_t) / ( norm(A_tilde) + norm(inp.archive.A_t) + cfg.numeric_tolerance)

NORMATIVE STATUS This module is exact within its declared computational scope. QGM computes bounded, non-negative internal route costs from versioned topology, density, resonance, and transport telemetry. GlyphNet maintains an internal application-layer routing domain, disseminates authenticated link-state records, computes deterministic shortest paths, forwards Glyph envelopes, and encapsulates external hops inside ordinary IPv4 plus TCP in the reference profile. It does not replace IPv4, BGP, OSPF, TCP, DNS, or the host operating-system network stack; it does not assign semantic meaning to public IPv4 octets; and it does not mutate archive, hysteresis, quarantine, RTSOM, RMX, or FBS state.

CLAIM BOUNDARY Quantum gravity, semantic gravity, gravitational potential, curl, vorticity, magnetic relaxation, archetypal seed, and glyph are architectural names. Their normative meanings are only the graph potential, bounded cost terms, circulation statistic, routing label, directory key, packet metadata, or typed custody request defined here. No claim is made that information density physically curves spacetime, that Internet latency is literal mass, or that standard routers interpret SpiralCore geometry. Ordinary routers see ordinary IPv4/TCP traffic between real endpoints; SpiralCore semantics remain inside the authenticated application payload.

1. Scope, Statement Classes, and Precedence GlyphNet is the internal routing protocol of a SpiralCore domain. It plays a role analogous to an interior routing protocol or an internal path-distribution system: nodes exchange topology and reachability information, compute next hops, and forward opaque Glyph payloads. When a next hop is outside the local process or chassis, the same Glyph frame is transported between actual network endpoints using the standard IPv4/TCP stack. The outer IP address identifies the remote host; the inner Glyph identifiers identify the SpiralCore route and payload.

2.2 Required execution order 1. Validate Module 4 configuration, DomainID, NodeID, control-plane key material, topology snapshot, and monotonic epoch state. 2. Authenticate and age link-state records; construct the canonical LSDB from the newest valid record per origin node. 3. Accept a sealed RouteIntentPacket from LORIEN or another explicitly authorized local service. 4. Resolve the logical destination to one or more candidate NodeIDs through the internal Glyph Directory. Use external DNS only to resolve configured node hostnames to real IPv4 endpoints. 5. Compute candidate resonance and QGM edge costs using one frozen topology/metric epoch. 6. Run deterministic shortest-path computation with stable tie-breaking and build a RouteDecisionPacket. 7. Construct one canonical GlyphEnvelope carrying full payload digest, compact GlyphLabel32, Q, chi, route intent, and internal hop limit. 8. If the destination is local, hand the envelope to the named local service adapter. If the next hop is internal, forward through the local adjacency. If remote, serialize a GNPFrame and send it to the actual peer IPv4 endpoint over TCP. 9. Validate delivery or transport result. Ordinary failures enter retry/degraded handling; only versioned custody policy may issue an RTSOMExhaustRequest. 10. Issue an FBSRecoveryRequest only for a catastrophic invariant defined in Section 7, never merely because the physical network is unavailable.

OUTER/INNER ADDRESS SEPARATION Outer IPv4 source and destination fields MUST contain real, configured, routable host endpoints. Region, Anchor, Phase, Identity, Cantor-derived labels, Q, chi, and vector data MUST remain inside the GNP application frame. The host network stack is never asked to route to an arbitrary semantic 32-bit value.

4.3 External IPv4/TCP encapsulation 1. Resolve the selected next-hop NodeID to a configured IPv4 endpoint and TCP port. 2. Open or reuse a standard TCP connection through the host network stack. The operating system selects ordinary source address, route, ARP/neighbor behavior, retransmission, congestion control, and outer IPv4 TTL. 3. Write a uint32 network-order frame length followed by the canonical GNPFrame bytes. 4. The peer reads exactly the declared length, verifies size bound, HMAC, payload digest, domain, route epoch, sequence, and inner destination. 5. The peer submits the inner envelope to GlyphNet forwarding or the local destination-service adapter. No semantic field is copied into the outer IPv4 address, DSCP, identification, fragment offset, or TCP port. The 32-bit GlyphLabel may be displayed in dotted-quad notation for debugging only, explicitly labeled GLYPH_LABEL, never IPV4_DESTINATION.

4.4 Q and chi preservation Q and chi are application metadata. Q preserves additive branch valuation and chi preserves the multiset of leaf modes. They are authenticated end-to-end across every hop and are not recomputed by intermediate routers unless a separately authorized transformation changes the payload and emits a new GlyphDigest. Q_parent = sum_j Q_child_j chi_parent = multiset_sum_j chi_child_j When L and H are carried, the receiver additionally verifies Q = 2L + 1 = H + 2. A scalar Q match does not prove structural equality; chi and the full branch digest remain required.

5. QGM Metric Mathematics QGM is formalized as a bounded graph-cost field. Let G_t = (V_t, E_t) be the authenticated GlyphNet topology at route epoch t. Every directed edge e=(i,j) has a positive administrative base cost and normalized telemetry. Every node may publish a bounded informational-density value rho_i derived by the authoritative producer.

b_ij                                       (0, +inf)                                   Administrative base cost; reference 1.0.

Normalized latency statistic under the ell_ij                                     [0,1] active profile.

p_ij                                       [0,1]                                       Observed loss/failure ratio.

q_ij                                       [0,1]                                       Queue or utilization pressure.

Read-only informational-density input for rho_i                                      [0,1] node i.

5.2 Bounded recursive potential phi_i(t+1) = clip(phi_decay_Q * phi_i(t) + (1 - phi_decay_Q) * rho_i(t), 0, 1) The factor (1 - phi_decay_Q) is normative. It corrects the legacy unbounded recurrence phi_next = 0.995 phi + rho, which can grow without limit for persistent positive rho. Under the formal recurrence, phi remains in [0,1] for all time when initialized in [0,1].

5.3 Glyph resonance cos_j = <x, a_j> / (||x||_2 ||a_j||_2) R_G(j,P) = clip((cos_j + 1) / 2, 0, 1)        If both vectors are nonzero, the equations above apply.        If both vectors are exactly zero, R_G = 1 only when the profile explicitly permits a zero anchor; the reference profile forbids zero anchors.        If exactly one vector is zero, R_G = 0.        A terminal AnchorID destination is eligible only when R_G >= tau_glyph. Intermediate forwarding nodes need not satisfy terminal resonance.

5.4 Edge cost The reference metric uses non-negative additive costs. Let the normalized attraction toward node j be a_ij = clip((phi_j - phi_i + 1)/2, 0, 1). Let weights be non-negative and sum to 1. The reference profile uses w_l=0.20, w_p=0.20, w_q=0.10, w_d=0.20, and w_r=0.30. c_ij(P,t) = b_ij * [1 + gamma_delta * (w_l ell_ij + w_p p_ij + w_q q_ij + w_d(1-a_ij) + w_r(1-R_G(j,P)))]

COST INVARIANT For finite normalized inputs, b_ij>0, 0<=gamma_delta<=1, and non-negative weights summing to 1, every c_ij is finite and strictly positive. Therefore deterministic Dijkstra/SPF is valid and no negative-cost cycle can be created by QGM.

5.5 Symbolic drift map N_d(i,j) = phi_j - phi_i

N_d is a directed potential difference used as one bounded cost feature. It is not a Euclidean gradient unless a continuous coordinate chart is separately defined. Positive N_d means the next node has higher potential; the reference attraction mapping lowers, but never negates, the edge cost.

5.6 Graph circulation / Phase-Gravitational Curl surrogate A pure scalar potential has zero circulation around a closed cycle. Routing asymmetry arises from directed telemetry and policy terms. Therefore the computable curl surrogate is defined from the antisymmetric residual of the final edge costs, not from the scalar potential alone. u_ij(P,t) = [c_ij(P,t) - c_ji(P,t)] / max(c_ij(P,t) + c_ji(P,t), epsilon) Curl_Q(C,P,t) = |sum_(i,j in C) u_ij(P,t)| / |C| Curl_Q_max(P,t) = max_(C in B_t) Curl_Q(C,P,t) B_t is a deterministic fundamental cycle basis of the current undirected topology, ordered lexicographically by NodeID. Curl_Q_max lies in [0,1]. It is telemetry for asymmetric circulation and route-instability diagnosis; it is not by itself an FBS trigger. Catastrophic escalation requires the persistent corruption conditions in Section 7.4.

6. GlyphNet Internal Control Plane (GN-LS) The reference profile is a signed link-state protocol inside one administrative SpiralCore domain. Its operational analogy is OSPF-like topology flooding with iBGP-like internal policy distribution; it is not wire-compatible with either protocol.

6.1 Adjacency and liveness 1. A node sends an authenticated HELLO containing DomainID, NodeID, profile digest, current route epoch, and monotonically increasing sequence. 2. A peer forms adjacency only when DomainID, profile, authentication, sequence freshness, and reciprocal endpoint policy are valid. 3. An adjacency is declared DOWN after dead_interval cycles without a valid HELLO. This produces a topology change, not an FBS event. 4. Loopback adjacencies are permitted only in MONO_LOOPBACK test mode and must be labeled MOCK_LINK.

6.2 Link-state acceptance Condition                                                        Action

6.3 Route-epoch construction route_epoch_digest = SHA256(canonical_sorted_LSDB || metric_profile_digest || directory_digest) The numerical route_epoch is a local monotonic counter. The digest is the authoritative topology identity. A route computation uses one immutable LSDB, directory, and MetricSnapshot; it may not mix records from different epochs.

6.4 Deterministic shortest-path computation 1. Build the directed graph from valid UP links in the frozen LSDB. 2. Remove nodes or links prohibited by route class, service policy, domain policy, expired records, or failed authentication. 3. For each eligible edge, compute c_ij(P,t) from the frozen MetricSnapshot and packet/anchor resonance. 4. Run Dijkstra from source NodeID. Compare path costs with numeric tolerance. If equal within tolerance, choose the lexicographically smaller full NodeID path. 5. For NodeID destinations, select the exact destination path. For ServiceID or AnchorID, select the eligible candidate with minimum path cost, then highest R_G, then lexicographically smallest NodeID. 6. Retain the existing valid route unless the new route improves normalized total cost by at least route_switch_margin, or the old route is invalid. 7. Seal the path, next hop, cost vector, epoch digest, and tie-break evidence in GlyphRouteDecision.

6.6 Hop limits and traces The inner hop limit begins at hop_limit_default and is decremented exactly once by every GlyphNet forwarding node. The outer IPv4 TTL is managed independently by the host network stack. A frame with inner hop_limit=0 is not forwarded. Its failure route is HOLD_NO_ROUTE or EXHAUST_REQUEST according to policy, not automatic FBS. route_trace_digest_(k+1) = SHA256(route_trace_digest_k || NodeID_k || sequence || route_epoch_digest) The compact trace digest detects divergent or repeated forwarding histories without carrying an unbounded path list. Debug profiles may carry a bounded explicit NodeID trace.

7.2 RTSOM custody delegation A failed frame may be converted into a bounded exhaust request only after the versioned retry policy is exhausted. The request carries the exact payload or immutable content reference, frame digest, route history digest, failure class, proposed mass, and no_delete=True. mass_proposal = ||decode_state(payload)||_2 (when the payload is a declared state vector) For opaque payloads, mass_proposal is a declared byte-domain statistic such as payload_length/max_frame_bytes and is labeled accordingly. Module 14 validates and owns the final mass definition. Until a matching RTSOM custody receipt is verified, Module 4 must retain the exact failed payload or immutable reference.

7.3 Spin-to-helicity surrogate The legacy polarity flip is retained only as optional failure metadata: failure_polarity_next = -failure_polarity_current. It does not alter the failed state vector, does not repair the network route, and does not prove preservation. The exact payload digest remains the custody identity.

12. Reference Pseudocode def update_qgm_potential(phi, rho, cfg): require_finite(phi, rho) require(0.0 <= phi <= 1.0 and 0.0 <= rho <= 1.0) return clip( cfg.phi_decay_q * phi + (1.0 - cfg.phi_decay_q) * rho, 0.0, 1.0)

def glyph_resonance(x, anchor, eps): nx, na = norm(x), norm(anchor) if nx <= eps or na <= eps: return 0.0 cosine = dot(x, anchor) / (nx * na) return clip((cosine + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0)

def edge_cost(link, phi_i, phi_j, resonance, cfg): require(link.base_cost > 0.0) require_all_unit_interval( link.latency, link.loss, link.queue, phi_i, phi_j, resonance) attraction = clip((phi_j - phi_i + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0) dynamic = ( cfg.w_latency * link.latency + cfg.w_loss * link.loss

def compute_glyph_route(intent, lsdb, directory, metrics, cfg): validate_intent_and_frozen_epoch(intent, lsdb, directory, metrics, cfg) candidates = directory.resolve(intent.destination_selector) graph = build_eligible_directed_graph(lsdb, intent.route_class)

best = None for destination in candidates: resonance = terminal_resonance(intent, destination) if destination.requires_anchor and resonance < cfg.tau_glyph: continue weighted_graph = apply_qgm_costs( graph, intent, destination, metrics, cfg) path, total, breakdown = deterministic_dijkstra( weighted_graph, cfg.numeric_tolerance) candidate = RouteCandidate( path=path, cost=total, resonance=resonance, destination=destination, breakdown=breakdown) best = deterministic_candidate_min(best, candidate)

if best is None: return GlyphRouteDecision(action="HOLD_NO_ROUTE") return seal_route_decision(intent, best, lsdb.epoch_digest)

def build_gnp_frame(intent, decision, payload, cfg): payload_digest = sha256(payload) glyph_digest = sha256(canonical_payload_and_route(payload, intent, decision)) metadata = canonical_sorted_tlvs( GLYPH_DIGEST=glyph_digest, INTENT_DIGEST=intent.intent_id, Q=encode_uint(intent.Q), CHI=encode_sorted_inventory(intent.chi), ROUTE_DECISION_DIGEST=decision.digest) frame_without_tag = serialize_network_order( magic=b"GNP1", version=1, domain_id=cfg.domain_id, route_epoch=decision.route_epoch, source_node_id=cfg.node_id, destination_node_id=decision.destination_node_id, glyph_label32=uint32(glyph_digest[:4]), hop_limit=cfg.hop_limit_default, metadata=metadata, payload=payload, payload_digest=payload_digest) tag = hmac_sha256(cfg.domain_key, frame_without_tag) return frame_without_tag + tag

def forward_frame(frame, route, transport, cfg): validate_frame(frame, cfg) if frame.destination_node_id == cfg.node_id: return local_service_delivery(frame) if frame.hop_limit == 0: return hold_failure("GN_HOP_LIMIT", frame)

next_frame = frame.with_hop_limit(frame.hop_limit - 1) next_frame = resign_frame(next_frame, cfg.domain_key) if route.next_hop.is_local: return route.next_hop.send(next_frame)

# Outer IPv4 endpoint is real infrastructure; no semantic octet mapping. endpoint = route.next_hop.ipv4_endpoint return transport.send_tcp_ipv4(endpoint, length_prefix(next_frame))

2.2 Atomic execution order 1. Freeze GuardianConfig, GuardianPolicy, TrustedAnchorSetSnapshot, GuardianStateSnapshot, and input packet digests for one evaluation epoch. 2. Validate versions, owner identifiers, signatures, dimensions, canonical serialization, and state compare-and-swap token. 3. Run Layer 1 syntax/canonicalization. A failure stops semantic math and emits a typed non-permit outcome. 4. Run Layer 2 anchor admission and Layer 3 symbolic/provenance checks. 5. Normalize affective telemetry and compute hard AFFECTIVE_LOCK before any weighted score can override it. 6. Compute C_guard, instantaneous drift, and provisional D_raw without changing persistent state. 7. Apply first-match route precedence and emit a canonical GuardianDecisionPacket. 8. Commit Guardian drift only after an authorized matching acknowledgement and only for the configured acceptance classes.

NO-COMMIT RULE Evaluation is side-effect free. A permit packet may carry a provisional GuardianStateUpdate, but persistent identity drift does not change until Guardian receives a matching downstream acknowledgement and successfully performs a compare-and-swap against the original state version.

NO REPAIR AT LAYER 1 Guardian MUST NOT reshape, truncate, fill missing values, replace NaN/Inf, clip out-of-range components, or rewrite metadata to make a malformed request pass. The exact original input is either evaluated as valid or routed as a non-permit outcome.

4.2 Layer 2 - Trusted-anchor admission For each authorized anchor a_j, compute cosine similarity using the exact finite vector X. s_j = <X, a_j> / (||X||_2 ||a_j||_2 + epsilon) j* = argmax_j (s_j, tie-break by lexicographic anchor_id) s_anchor = s_j*    and     anchor_gap = s_(1) - s_(2)       If ||X||_2 <= epsilon, the reference profile emits G_SEM_ZERO_VECTOR. A policy may define a dedicated null anchor, but it must be explicit and versioned.       If no authorized anchor is active for the packet domain/role, emit G_SEM_NO_ANCHOR.       If s_anchor < TAU_ANCHOR, route as UNRESOLVED_ANCHOR. This is a policy-relative hold/quarantine reason, not a claim of maliciousness or falsehood.       anchor_gap is telemetry for ambiguity. The reference profile does not deny solely on a small gap if the winning score passes, but policies may require review.

4.3 Layer 3 - Symbolic and provenance integrity Hard symbolic checks are evaluated as a finite Boolean vector. The topology score is a separately versioned soft metric. h = (canonical_ok + digest_ok + owner_ok + sequence_ok + q_chi_ok + route_class_ok) / 6 S_symbol = 0.60 h + 0.40 topology_score Any zero in digest_ok, owner_ok, sequence_ok, q_chi_ok, or route_class_ok is a hard symbolic failure even when S_symbol would otherwise be high. canonical_ok is already required by Layer 1 but is repeated in the packet for cross- owner audit.

4.4 Reference topology-score provider When the active TAS supplies an orthogonal projector P for the permitted symbolic subspace, the reference provider computes a normalized projection score: r_top = ||X - P X||_2 / (||X||_2 + epsilon) topology_score = clip(1 - r_top, 0, 1) If P is absent, malformed, non-idempotent, or incompatible with DIM, Guardian emits a configuration fault rather than inventing a Hodge or topology result. Alternative providers are permitted only with an explicit algorithm_id and conformance tests.

5. Affective-Risk Surrogate and Preliminary Coherence The EmotionTensor is internal system telemetry. Guardian treats valence, arousal, and baseline coherence as bounded control signals; it does not infer a person's emotions or intent.

5.1 Normalization a = clip(arousal, 0, 1) v_norm = clip((valence + 1) / 2, 0, 1) xi = clip(Xi, 0, 1) calm = 1 - a anchor_norm = clip((s_anchor + 1) / 2, 0, 1)

5.2 Hard affective lock affective_lock = (a > 0.80) AND (xi < 0.50) This preserves the original hard-bound intent while changing the label from a human panic diagnosis to a computational AFFECTIVE_LOCK. The comparator boundaries are strict: a=0.80 or xi=0.50 does not trigger this lock.

5.3 Corrected preliminary coherence score The legacy formula added arousal directly, allowing a more excited packet to receive a higher pass score. The formal profile uses calmness instead and incorporates the declared anchor and symbolic layers. C_guard = 0.25 xi + 0.25 anchor_norm + 0.20 S_symbol + 0.15 v_norm + 0.15 calm

SCORE RANGE Every component lies in [0,1], every weight is non-negative, and the weights sum to 1. Therefore C_guard lies in [0,1]. C_guard >= 0.85 is necessary but never sufficient: all hard syntax, symbolic, authorization, replay, affective- lock, and drift conditions must also pass.

5.4 Legacy score handling C_legacy = (arousal + v_norm + xi) / 3 C_legacy may be emitted only as migration telemetry under algorithm_id="GUARDIAN_LEGACY_V14". It MUST NOT authorize a route in v14.1 because its arousal sign conflicts with the declared safety interpretation.

6. Identity Sphere Drift as a Versioned Ledger Identity drift is formalized as a bounded-risk accumulator with decay and two-phase commit. It measures policy- relative deviation from the current approved reference state; it is not a measure of a person's identity or psychological stability.

6.1 Glyph density rho_raw = (1 / DIM) sum_i |X_i| rho_hat = rho_raw / (rho_raw + RHO_SCALE) For finite X and RHO_SCALE>0, rho_hat lies in [0,1). A different density provider requires a versioned algorithm_id; raw embedding indices are not accepted without a defined normalization.

6.2 Phase mismatch d_phase = (1 - cos(wrap(phi_em - phi_anchor))) / 2 d_phase lies in [0,1]. If the winning anchor has no reference phase, the reference profile sets the phase-density term to zero and records PHASE_NOT_APPLICABLE; it does not invent a phase.

6.3 Instantaneous drift d_anchor = clip((1 - s_anchor) / 2, 0, 1) d_symbol = 1 - S_symbol r_affect = a (1 - xi) d_inst = clip(0.35 d_anchor + 0.20 rho_hat d_phase + 0.25 d_symbol + 0.20 r_affect, 0, 1)

6.4 Provisional accumulator update D_raw = LAMBDA_ID D_t + GAMMA_GUARD d_inst permit_drift = (D_raw <= DELTA_ID_MAX) The reference values LAMBDA_ID=0.98 and GAMMA_GUARD=0.10 permit recovery toward zero under sustained low deviation while allowing repeated high-deviation events to exhaust the budget. D_raw is evaluated before clipping. A denied or unacknowledged packet does not alter D_t.

6.5 Two-phase drift commit 1. Guardian emits GuardianStateUpdate(old_version, proposed_delta_id=D_raw, decision_digest). 2. The configured downstream owner emits an acceptance receipt bound to request_id and decision_digest. 3. Guardian verifies the receipt, current state version, policy digest, TAS digest, and idempotency key. 4. Guardian atomically commits proposed_delta_id and increments state_version exactly once. 5. A duplicate receipt returns the prior commit result. A stale state version emits G_STATE_CAS_CONFLICT and does not overwrite newer state.

8.2 What INERT_GLYPH means       The quarantined envelope cannot be executed, routed, compiled, merged, repaired, or archived as an accepted state.       The original payload digest, provenance, and diagnostic evidence remain available to authorized review tooling.       INERT_GLYPH does not assert maliciousness. The reason class distinguishes malformed, unresolved, unauthorized, duplicate/replayed, and risk-bound outcomes.       Release requires a new signed policy/review decision and a new Guardian evaluation; a quarantine tag is never stripped in place.

8.3 Capacity and backpressure A full or unavailable quarantine service is an operational capacity failure. Guardian MUST stop accepting new work for the affected boundary, preserve pending request references, and emit QUARANTINE_BACKPRESSURE. It MUST NOT route the payload to /dev/null, overwrite an older quarantined object, or automatically invoke FBS merely because storage is full.

8.4 RTSOM delegation A later policy may request that an exact, custody-confirmed quarantine residue contribute to the RTSOM bounded exhaust model. That operation requires a separate RTSOMExhaustRequest and matching receipt. Guardian does not convert a denied payload into mass and does not mutate S_mu_nu.
