9.2 TAS and policy publication 1. A new policy or TAS is assembled offline or by an authorized configuration compiler. 2. All vectors, projectors, roles, thresholds, weights, validity intervals, and compatibility constraints are validated. 3. The publisher signs the canonical snapshot and assigns a monotone version. 4. Guardian loads the snapshot only at a quiescent boundary or through an atomic epoch swap. 5. In-flight evaluations retain the old immutable snapshot; no request is evaluated partly under two policy versions. 6. State migration must explicitly name old/new policy and TAS digests. Silent reinterpretation of delta_id is prohibited.

9.3 Determinism and serialization       All floats are finite float64. Comparisons use declared strict/inclusive operators; no hidden rounding to displayed decimals.       Arrays are serialized in canonical dimension order, canonical byte order, and a declared float encoding before hashing.       Maps use sorted canonical keys; optional fields use explicit null markers.       Decision and state digests include module, algorithm, policy, TAS, input, and prior-state versions.       Wall-clock timestamps are metadata only and MUST NOT change a deterministic decision. Logical time and sequence numbers control validity.

function guardian_evaluate(input, config, policy, tas, state): frozen = freeze_and_hash(input, config, policy, tas, state) validate_snapshot_compatibility(frozen)          # no mutation

syntax = check_syntax_and_canonicalization(input, config) if not syntax.pass: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, syntax.codes, "MALFORMED")

hard = check_provenance_and_symbolic_hard_fields(input) if not hard.pass: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, hard.codes, "INTEGRITY_OR_POLICY_DENIED")

anchor = select_authorized_anchor(input.X, tas, input.domain, input.role) if not anchor.exists or anchor.score < config.TAU_ANCHOR: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, anchor.codes, "UNRESOLVED_ANCHOR")

a        = clip(input.emotion.arousal, 0, 1) v_norm   = clip((input.emotion.valence + 1) / 2, 0, 1) xi       = clip(input.baseline_coherence, 0, 1) calm     = 1 - a a_norm   = clip((anchor.score + 1) / 2, 0, 1)

affective_lock = (a > config.AROUSAL_LOCK) and

(xi < config.COHERENCE_LOCK) if affective_lock: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, ["G_AFFECTIVE_LOCK"], "AFFECTIVE_LOCK")

topology_score = compute_versioned_topology_score(input.X, anchor.projector) h = mean([ input.symbolic.canonical_ok, input.symbolic.digest_ok, input.symbolic.owner_ok, input.symbolic.sequence_ok, input.symbolic.q_chi_ok, input.symbolic.route_class_ok ]) S_symbol = 0.60*h + 0.40*topology_score

C_guard = 0.25*xi + 0.25*a_norm + 0.20*S_symbol + \ 0.15*v_norm + 0.15*calm

rho_raw = mean(abs(input.X)) rho_hat = rho_raw / (rho_raw + config.RHO_SCALE) d_phase = phase_distance(input.phi_em, anchor.reference_phase) d_anchor = clip((1 - anchor.score)/2, 0, 1) d_symbol = 1 - S_symbol r_affect = a*(1 - xi) d_inst = clip(0.35*d_anchor + 0.20*rho_hat*d_phase + 0.25*d_symbol + 0.20*r_affect, 0, 1) D_raw = config.LAMBDA_ID*state.delta_id + config.GAMMA_GUARD*d_inst

if D_raw > config.DELTA_ID_MAX: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, ["G_DRIFT_LIMIT"], "IDENTITY_DRIFT_LIMIT") if C_guard < config.C_GUARD_MIN: return seal_quarantine(input, frozen, ["G_SCORE_LOW"], "PRELIMINARY_COHERENCE_LOW")

route = route_for_boundary(input.boundary_profile, input) update = provisional_state_update(state.version, D_raw, frozen.decision_basis) return seal_decision(route, metrics, update, frozen)

function guardian_commit(decision, receipt, current_state): require receipt.request_id == decision.request_id require receipt.decision_digest == decision.digest require decision.provisional_update.old_version == current_state.version require receipt.owner in configured_commit_owners return atomic_compare_and_swap(current_state, decision.provisional_update)

function seal_quarantine(input, frozen, codes, reason_class): request = QuarantineRequest( payload_digest=frozen.payload_digest, payload_reference=input.immutable_reference, reason_codes=codes, reason_class=reason_class, capability_mask=NONE, proposed_tag="INERT_GLYPH" ) return GuardianDecisionPacket(route=QUARANTINE_REQUEST, request=request, state_update=None, frozen=frozen)

They receive frozen values and return values plus algorithm identifiers; they do not log, mutate state, or route.    Use custom typed exceptions or Result records. A catch-all exception MUST NOT be converted into quarantine or FBS because that hides implementation bugs.    Store decision evidence as digests plus bounded diagnostic fields. Do not duplicate large vectors in every log when an immutable content reference exists.    Treat policy, TAS, and state as immutable objects. Replace snapshots atomically rather than editing arrays in place.    Keep legacy C_pass telemetry behind an explicit feature flag and never use it for authorization.    Unit-test strict comparator boundaries with nextafter values, not only decimal literals.

NORMATIVE STATUS This module is exact within its declared computational scope. It selects an immutable tail of accepted state records, constructs the sample covariance matrix, performs a symmetric eigendecomposition, measures the fraction of total variance carried by the dominant principal component, packages readiness and numerical diagnostics, and returns one immutable CVCMetricPacket to the Sigma-Lattice. It does not evaluate the current candidate directly, choose an architectural route, repair a state, tighten an attractor, mutate archive history, write to HARMONY or RTSOM, or execute FBS recovery.

CLAIM BOUNDARY CVC is a principal-variance concentration statistic. A high value establishes that accepted historical fluctuations are concentrated along one empirical covariance direction under this profile. It does not prove factual truth, semantic correctness, flat-minimum optimization, a Hodge-theoretic invariant, biological coherence, or a literal low- dimensional physical manifold. Those interpretations remain hypotheses or separately versioned providers.

2. Architecture Role and Lifecycle Sigma invokes CVC after a candidate RMF is available and before aggregate route arbitration. CVC ignores the candidate vector and reads only the accepted-history snapshot. This prevents a rejected proposal from contaminating the reference covariance used to judge future proposals.

2.1 Required execution order 1. Validate CVCConfig, Boot/profile binding, backend profile, and tolerance ordering. 2. Validate all AcceptedStateRecord entries, cycle monotonicity, dimension, finite float64 values, and accepted-status provenance. 3. Select the newest min(W, N_history) records without changing their chronological order. 4. Compute the canonical window digest before numerical work. 5. If n < 2, emit WARMING with no covariance or eigenvalue claim. 6. Compute the row mean and mean-centered history matrix. 7. Construct the unbiased sample covariance matrix using divisor n-1. 8. Symmetrize only to remove floating-point asymmetry and record the correction norm. 9. Run the declared symmetric eigensolver and validate its finite, sorted, positive-semidefinite spectrum. 10. Classify zero-variance degeneracy or compute CVC and diagnostics from the nonnegative spectrum. 11. Seal provenance, readiness, threshold flags, metrics, backend identity, and digest in CVCMetricPacket.

4.2 Exact threshold storage The source describes the CVC threshold as exactly two-thirds while writing 0.66. The normative profile stores 2/3 as a rational configuration value and serializes it canonically. A value equal to 2/3 meets the threshold; a value one representable unit below it does not.

4.3 Meaning of low dominance CVC < 0.20 means that no single principal component carries 20 percent of the measured variance. It is named LOW_DOMINANCE_ALERT. It does not, by itself, prove isotropy. True isotropy is a distributional statement about the complete eigenvalue spectrum; the dashboard therefore also reports effective rank and eigenvalue entropy.

5. Accepted-History Window Selection and Canonicalization 5.1 Selection rule Let H be the complete accepted-history snapshot in strictly increasing cycle order. The selected window H_W is the newest min(W, |H|) records. Selection is by accepted cycle, not arrival timestamp, filename order, storage position, or candidate similarity. H_W = tail_W(H) n = |H_W| = min(W, |H|)

5.2 Candidate exclusion The raw Delta candidate, a Guardian-admitted packet, a HARMONY repair candidate, and any state without an Archivist commit digest are excluded. Changing the current proposal while holding accepted history constant MUST leave the CVCMetricPacket unchanged except for request-cycle and upstream-correlation fields.

5.3 Canonical window digest 1. Encode profile version, DIM, W, session ID, snapshot ID, and selected cycle range using the canonical serialization version. 2. For each record in chronological order, encode cycle, state_digest, commit_digest, profile_digest, accepted flag, and the presence/value of rmf_on_accept. 3. Encode raw state values as IEEE-754 binary64 in declared byte order, even when a matching state_digest is supplied. 4. Hash the complete byte stream using SHA-256 to obtain window_digest. A state record with an unchanged display value but changed canonical bits is a different window. Duplicate cycle numbers, nonmonotonic chronology, or digest mismatches are faults rather than silently repaired history.

6. Exact Mathematical Mechanics 6.1 Mean and centered history matrix For n >= 2, stack selected states as rows of S in R^(n x D). Let 1_n be the length-n all-ones vector. mu = (1/n) * sum_{i=1..n} s_i Y = S - 1_n * mu^T Centering makes the covariance and spectrum invariant to adding the same finite offset vector to every accepted state.

6.2 Unbiased sample covariance Sigma_raw = (Y^T Y) / (n - 1) Sigma = (Sigma_raw + Sigma_raw^T) / 2 The second line removes only floating-point asymmetry. It is not a denoising operator. The symmetry correction norm and pre-correction asymmetry norm are recorded. Any configured asymmetry limit breach is a numerical fault.

6.3 Symmetric eigendecomposition Sigma = U diag(lambda_1, ..., lambda_D) U^T lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_D The reference implementation uses a dense symmetric eigensolver equivalent to LAPACK SYEVD/SYEVR through a versioned backend. It does not solve det(Sigma - lambda I) symbolically. Eigenvectors are not required in the packet because their signs are arbitrary, and repeated eigenvalues make individual basis vectors non-unique.

6.4 Positive-semidefinite validation and clipping tau_psd = eigen_abs_tol + eigen_rel_tol * max(1, lambda_max_abs, |trace(Sigma)|)    Any eigenvalue less than -tau_psd produces CVC_NEGATIVE_SPECTRUM_FAULT.    Eigenvalues in [-tau_psd, 0) are clipped to zero as roundoff artifacts.    The count and absolute clipped mass are recorded. They are never hidden.    After clipping, eigenvalues are sorted descending and total variance is recomputed from the nonnegative spectrum.

6.5 Zero-variance floor scale_2 = max(1, mean_i ||s_i||_2^2, ||mu||_2^2) tau_var = variance_abs_tol + variance_rel_tol * scale_2 V_total = sum_{k=1..D} lambda_k = trace(Sigma) If V_total <= tau_var, the window is DEGENERATE. The reference packet records CVC = 0, numerical_rank = 0, effective_rank = 0, threshold_met = false, and degenerate_zero_variance = true. Zero variance is not one-dimensional collapse because no varying direction exists.

6.6 Correlated Variance Coherence CVC = lambda_1 / V_total, for V_total > tau_var No epsilon is added to the denominator after nondegeneracy is established. This preserves the exact principal- variance fraction and threshold semantics.

6.7 Spectral diagnostics gap_absolute = lambda_1 - lambda_2, with lambda_2 = 0 when D = 1 gap_fraction = (lambda_1 - lambda_2) / V_total top_two_ratio = lambda_1 / lambda_2, when lambda_2 > tau_var; else +infinity p_k = lambda_k / V_total effective_rank = exp(-sum_{p_k>0} p_k * ln(p_k))

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 6 / CVC Spectral Measurement Contract

numerical_rank = count(lambda_k > rank_rel_tol * lambda_1) The bounded dashboard spectral gap is gap_fraction. top_two_ratio is reported separately because it is unbounded and becomes infinite for a rank-one spectrum.

6.8 Historical RMF diagnostic For source compatibility, Module 6 reports the mean of all non-null rmf_on_accept values inside the selected window. This is historical evidence only. rho_RMF_historical = mean({rmf_on_accept_i | value is present}) Sigma owns the route-authoritative prospective mean. It appends the current candidate RMF to the newest W-1 accepted RMFs without accepting the candidate. Module 6 does not compute or gate on that prospective value.

ROUTING BOUNDARY COLLAPSE_VALIDATED and VARIANCE_RECONSTRUCT_FAIL are evidence reason codes, not executable handoffs. Only Sigma emits PHASE_LIFT_REQUEST, BRAIDBACK_REQUEST, SEAL, or FBS_RECOVERY_REQUEST. Module 6 does not call Delta, HARMONY, RTSOM, the Archivist, or FBS directly.

9. Numerical Profile, Determinism, and Complexity 9.1 Reference backend         All state, mean, centered matrix, covariance, and eigenvalue calculations use IEEE-754 binary64.         The dense reference profile uses a symmetric eigensolver; generic nonsymmetric eigensolvers are nonconforming.         The covariance matrix is formed explicitly for D=81. A Gram-matrix or SVD profile may be added later only with a distinct profile ID and equivalence tests.         Thread count, backend vendor/version, compiler flags, and floating-point environment are recorded for reproducibility.         Within one pinned backend profile, canonical output is expected to be byte-deterministic. Across conforming backends, scalar metrics are tolerance-conformant rather than guaranteed bit-identical.

9.2 Eigenvector ambiguity Eigenvector signs are arbitrary. When eigenvalues are repeated or nearly repeated, the basis inside the associated eigenspace is also arbitrary. Therefore routing must not depend on a raw eigenvector sign or column ordering. If a future module requires a dominant subspace, it must consume a sign-invariant projector or a separately canonicalized subspace packet.

9.3 Complexity Time = O(n D^2 + D^3) Memory = O(n D + D^2) For the reference profile n=100 and D=81, dense computation is deliberate and testable. Any approximate, randomized, streaming, or sparse variant must declare its error model, seeds, confidence bounds, and new profile ID.

12.2 Property-based tests         For random finite accepted windows, the covariance is symmetric within tolerance and all sealed eigenvalues are nonnegative.         For every nondegenerate window, 0 < CVC <= 1, 0 <= gap_fraction <= 1, and rank <= min(D,n-1).         Translation, common nonzero scaling, orthogonal transformation, and dimension permutation preserve CVC within tolerance.         Changing an unaccepted candidate cannot change CVC numerical fields.         Appending accepted records beyond W changes the window only when a newer record enters the selected tail.         Round-trip canonical serialization preserves every normative field and packet digest.

12.3 Fuzz and stress requirements         Fuzz malformed shapes, enormous but finite values inside/outside the domain, NaNs, infinities, duplicate cycles, digest corruption, and truncated records.         Stress at least 100,000 deterministic windows across rank-one, equal-rank, slowly rotating, stationary, low- amplitude, and adversarially ill-conditioned fixtures.         Run concurrency tests proving immutable snapshot semantics and no cross-attempt state leakage.         Run backend parity tests on all supported BLAS/LAPACK profiles, recording maximum scalar deviation and clipping differences.         Inject eigensolver failures and timeouts; verify typed CVCFault without FBS, HARMONY, or RTSOM mutation.

13. Reference Pseudocode def cvc_measure(inp, cfg): validate_config_and_binding(inp, cfg) records = validate_accepted_history(inp.accepted_history, cfg) window = records[-cfg.window_size:] window_digest = canonical_window_digest(window, inp, cfg) n = len(window)

if n == 0: return seal_packet(status="EMPTY", cvc=None, ready=False, ...) if n == 1: return seal_packet(status="WARMING_SINGLETON", cvc=None, ready=False, ...)

S = rows([record.state for record in window], dtype=float64) mu = mean(S, axis=0, dtype=float64) Y = S - mu cov_raw = (Y.T @ Y) / float(n - 1) asymmetry = norm(cov_raw - cov_raw.T, ord="fro") validate_asymmetry(asymmetry, cov_raw, cfg) cov = 0.5 * (cov_raw + cov_raw.T)

Page 16

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 6 / CVC Spectral Measurement Contract

eigenvalues = symmetric_eigvalsh(cov, backend=cfg.backend_id) validate_finite(eigenvalues) tau_psd = cfg.eigen_abs_tol + cfg.eigen_rel_tol * max( 1.0, max(abs(eigenvalues)), abs(trace(cov))) if min(eigenvalues) < -tau_psd: raise CVCFault("NEGATIVE_SPECTRUM") clipped = clip(eigenvalues, 0.0, +inf) lambdas = sort_descending(clipped)

total = sum(lambdas) scale2 = max(1.0, mean(row_norm_squared(S)), dot(mu, mu)) tau_var = cfg.variance_abs_tol + cfg.variance_rel_tol * scale2 if total <= tau_var: return seal_packet( status="DEGENERATE", cvc=0.0, numerical_rank=0, effective_rank=0.0, threshold_met=False, ...)

cvc = lambdas[0] / total gap_fraction = (lambdas[0] - lambdas[1]) / total p = [x / total for x in lambdas if x > 0.0] effective_rank = exp(-sum(x * log(x) for x in p)) numerical_rank = count(x > cfg.rank_rel_tol * lambdas[0] for x in lambdas) full_ready = n == cfg.window_size

return seal_packet( status="READY" if full_ready else "DIAGNOSTIC", cvc=cvc, threshold_met=full_ready and cvc >= Fraction(2, 3), low_dominance_alert=full_ready and cvc < 0.20, route_authoritative_ready=full_ready, window_digest=window_digest, commit_performed=False, ...)

It validates one versioned symbolic-feature packet, computes the CSIGMA mean-product score, compares one Delta proposal with one archive feature-map snapshot using a bounded residual-contrast metric, derives a bounded exploration-fuel proposal when residual pressure is active, measures angular phase-reference drift from accepted phase history, and emits one immutable SymbolicParadoxPacket to the Sigma-Lattice. 4.1 Meaning of CSIGMA The score measures average signed agreement between nonnegative symbolic support S and signed valence/support direction V. It is bounded and reproducible when the provider packet is valid. Its meaning is conditional on the

Page 7

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 7 / CSIGMA and Paradox Evidence Contract

provider. A provider trained or configured badly can produce a precise but invalid score; provenance and calibration therefore remain mandatory.

4.2 Meaning of paradox pressure The name G_t is retained for architecture compatibility, but the normative quantity is a bounded archive-residual contrast. A negative value means the distance between the proposal and the archive feature map exceeds the proposal norm under the declared common feature scale. It is evidence of strong novelty or mismatch, not proof of logical contradiction or incompleteness.

4.3 Meaning of identity drift Delta_Xi is normalized angular displacement between the current computational phase direction and a reference direction formed from accepted phase history. It is not a statement about a human identity, personality, intention, diagnosis, or mental state. The value 0.20 corresponds to 0.20*pi radians, or 36 degrees, in the reference profile.

5. Input Validation and Canonicalization 5.1 Cross-packet consistency    All packets must share session_id, cycle, Boot profile digest, DIM, feature domain, and scale profile where applicable.    The symbolic packet candidate_digest must equal the Delta proposal digest.    The archive feature source cycle must not exceed the proposal cycle.    Phase history may include only accepted committed records preceding the current proposal.    Any digest mismatch is a fault. Module 7 must not recompute, repair, substitute, or silently rebind upstream data.

5.2 Numeric domain validation    X_proposal and F_A must be finite float64 arrays of exact length DIM.    S must be finite, length DIM, and componentwise inside [0,1].    V must be finite, length DIM, and componentwise inside [-1,1].    Phase vectors must be finite length-3 arrays. AVAILABLE phase vectors must have norm greater than epsilon_norm.    Inputs outside their declared domain are faults; Module 7 performs no hidden clipping.

5.3 Canonical serialization 1. Encode field names and values in the canonical schema order. 2. Encode integers using unsigned or signed fixed-width network byte order as declared by the schema. 3. Encode float64 values using raw IEEE-754 binary64 bits in declared byte order. 4. Encode arrays with explicit length and shape before raw element bytes. 5. Encode optional fields using an explicit presence tag. 6. Hash the complete byte stream using SHA-256. Display formatting, decimal text, JSON key order, and platform-native NaN encodings are not canonical inputs. NaN and infinity are invalid before serialization.

6. Exact Mathematical Mechanics 6.1 CSIGMA mean-product score Let D = DIM. The reference profile uses nonnegative symbolic support S_i in [0,1] and signed valence/support V_i in [-1,1]. C_SIGMA = (1/D) * sum_{i=1..D} S_i * V_i -1 <= C_SIGMA <= 1

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 7 / CSIGMA and Paradox Evidence Contract

The inclusive pass evidence flag is true when C_SIGMA >= 0.85. The terminal symbolic evidence flag is true when C_SIGMA < 0.50. Equality at 0.50 is not terminal; equality at 0.85 meets pass evidence.

6.2 Support diagnostics support_mean = (1/D) * sum_{i=1..D} S_i C_active = sum_i S_i * V_i / sum_i S_i, when sum_i S_i > epsilon_norm C_active is a diagnostic average over active support mass. If the support sum is at or below epsilon_norm, C_active is null and C_SIGMA remains exactly zero. C_active never replaces C_SIGMA in the Sigma route profile.

6.3 Archive residual and bounded G metric r = X_proposal - F(A_t) n_x = ||X_proposal||_2,   n_r = ||r||_2 The source formula divided by ||X_proposal|| plus epsilon, which becomes arbitrarily negative near a zero proposal. The normative profile uses a bounded contrast with the same sign interpretation. G_t = (n_x - n_r) / (n_x + n_r + epsilon_norm) Special case: when n_x <= epsilon_norm and n_r <= epsilon_norm, define G_t = 1.0. Otherwise G_t lies in [-1,1]. G_t < 0 exactly when n_r > n_x, subject only to the explicit both-zero policy. paradox_pressure = max(0, -G_t) The migration-only legacy diagnostic may be reported as 1 - n_r/n_x only when n_x > epsilon_norm. It is null otherwise and never participates in routing or fuel generation.

6.4 Bounded exploration-fuel proposal Fuel is generated only from active residual pressure. The residual direction is normalized by its infinity norm to remove unit-scale dependence. r_scale = max(||r||_infinity, epsilon_norm) u_r = r / r_scale H_G = paradox_pressure * zeta * tanh(kappa * u_r), when G_t < 0 H_G = 0, when G_t >= 0 |H_G[i]| <= paradox_pressure * zeta <= zeta H_G is a proposal packet. It is not automatically added to the candidate, archive, hysteresis, or exhaust budget. A downstream owner must explicitly accept custody.

6.5 Phase-reference construction Select the newest min(phase_window, N) accepted phase records. Normalize each nonzero vector to unit length. u_j = Xi_j / ||Xi_j||_2 m = (1/K) * sum_{j=1..K} u_j R_phase = ||m||_2 R_phase is the directional concentration. Drift is ready only when K >= phase_reference_min_count and R_phase > epsilon_norm. A near-zero mean means accepted directions cancel and no unique reference direction exists. u_ref = m / R_phase u_now = Xi_now / ||Xi_now||_2

6.6 Normalized angular identity drift Delta_Xi = arccos(clip(<u_now, u_ref>, -1, 1)) / pi 0 <= Delta_Xi <= 1

drift_alert is true only when drift_ready is true and Delta_Xi > drift_limit. Equality at 0.20 does not trigger the alert. If the reference is unavailable or directionally ambiguous, Delta_Xi is null and drift_alert is false with an explicit not- ready reason.

NO LOCAL ROUTE TREE Module 7 does not read PDV, RMF, CVC, tau_eff, or tortuosity and therefore cannot reproduce the complete Sigma decision. Module 2 receives this packet and applies the authoritative first-match route precedence. This eliminates the legacy conflict in which Module 2 and Module 7 each claimed to be the final arbiter.

10.1 Property and metamorphic tests         For all valid S and V, C_SIGMA remains in [-1,1].         Permuting S and V by the same index permutation leaves C_SIGMA, support_mean, and C_active unchanged.         Multiplying candidate and archive features by the same positive scalar leaves bounded G unchanged, except at explicit norm-floor boundaries.         H_G is odd in the normalized residual direction when paradox_pressure is held fixed.         Orthogonal rotation of all phase vectors leaves normalized angular drift unchanged.         Adding rejected or uncommitted phase records cannot change the accepted phase snapshot used by Module 7.         Changing RMF, CVC, PDV, or tortuosity outside Module 7 cannot change its packet because those inputs are absent from the contract.

10.2 Stress and fuzz requirements         At least 100,000 random finite attempts across zero, subnormal, ordinary, and near-boundary values.         Structured fuzzing of dimensions, lengths, digests, provider identifiers, cycles, and canonical field ordering.         Adversarial numeric cases including huge finite common scales, cancellation in phase means, sparse S, saturated V, and near-zero residual norms.         Concurrency tests proving that parallel invocations cannot cross-bind providers, phase snapshots, or candidate digests.         Fault injection at each validation, calculation, serialization, and return stage with proof of no partial output or state mutation.

11. Reference Pseudocode def module7_attempt(inp, cfg): validate_module7_input(inp, cfg)

x = readonly_float64(inp.delta_packet.X_proposal) f = readonly_float64(inp.archive_feature_packet.F_A) s = readonly_float64(inp.symbolic_feature_packet.S) v = readonly_float64(inp.symbolic_feature_packet.V)

csigma = mean(s * v)

support_mean = mean(s) support_sum = sum(s) csigma_active = (sum(s * v) / support_sum if support_sum > cfg.epsilon_norm else None)

residual = x - f nx = norm2(x) nr = norm2(residual) if nx <= cfg.epsilon_norm and nr <= cfg.epsilon_norm: g = 1.0 else: g = (nx - nr) / (nx + nr + cfg.epsilon_norm) pressure = max(0.0, -g)

if g < 0.0: r_scale = max(norm_inf(residual), cfg.epsilon_norm) h_g = pressure * cfg.zeta * tanh(cfg.kappa * residual / r_scale) else: r_scale = max(norm_inf(residual), cfg.epsilon_norm) h_g = zeros(cfg.dim)

phase = phase_drift(inp.phase_reference_packet, cfg)

evidence = { 'pass_evidence': csigma >= cfg.csigma_pass, 'symbolic_nullify_evidence': csigma < cfg.csigma_pass, 'terminal_symbolic_evidence': csigma < cfg.csigma_terminal, 'paradox_active': g < 0.0, 'terminal_recovery_evidence': ( g < 0.0 and csigma < cfg.csigma_terminal), 'phase_drift_evidence': ( phase.ready and phase.delta_xi > cfg.drift_limit), 'evidence_only': True, }

return seal_symbolic_paradox_packet( csigma=csigma, csigma_active=csigma_active, support_mean=support_mean, bounded_g=g, paradox_pressure=pressure, h_g=h_g, phase=phase, evidence=evidence, route_selected=None, state_mutated=False, ...)

NORMATIVE STATUS This module is exact within its declared computational scope. LORIEN validates one Sigma-authorized state against one committed predecessor and one immutable passive-chassis route reference; computes structural novelty, cross-chassis synchronization, transition shear, logical anchor intent, internal phase-band shift, and a cycle- bounded temporal window; then emits one sealed RouteIntentPacket, repair request, hold packet, or fault. It does not compute network paths, maintain a routing table, encapsulate an outer IPv4 packet, open a socket, write an archive record, perform Braidback repair, mutate quarantine or exhaust state, or execute FBS recovery.

CLAIM BOUNDARY “Active chassis,” “passive chassis,” “seed resonance,” “subnet shift,” and “ontological routing” are architectural names for explicit runtime roles and numerical metadata. LORIEN is not a NAT implementation, DNS server, Internet routing protocol, neurological model, or proof that latency becomes physical mass. The module produces logical route intent. Module 4 QGM/GlyphNet owns internal topology resolution and forwarding; the host stack owns ordinary IPv4/TCP transport.

1. Scope, Statement Classes, and Precedence LORIEN is the state-specific route-intent and indexing layer. It begins only after Sigma has authorized a candidate with route SEAL. It binds that candidate to accepted history, a passive archive reference, a logical destination policy, a temporal validity interval, and deterministic anchor metadata. The resulting packet is an instruction to the routing owner; it is not itself a route, delivery, archive commit, or semantic approval.

1.3 Explicit non-goals       No conversion of a semantic 32-bit value into an outer Internet destination address.       No direct DNS query for an archetype, no kernel routing-table change, and no socket transmission.       No claim that SHA-256 produces a semantically correct destination; hashing provides deterministic distribution under a declared policy.       No claim that a 32-bit label is unique or reversible to the original state vector.       No direct Braidback, phase lift, archive commit, quarantine, RTSOM mutation, Cantor diagonalization, or Collatz fold.       No automatic FBS event for low synchronization, high shear, missing anchors, stale references, or ordinary routing unavailability.

2. Architecture Role, Profiles, and Lifecycle The source module combined five distinct concerns: state/reference geometry, logical indexing, network addressing, external transport, and recovery. The formal profile retains the first two and the temporal policy. Network routing and transport are delegated to Module 4; boundary authorization is delegated to Guardian; repair and recovery remain with their authoritative owners.

2.3 Required execution order 1. Validate LorienConfig against Boot profile and Module 4 RouteIntent schema version. 2. Validate the Sigma SEAL decision, candidate digest, candidate vector, structural identity, and session/cycle bindings. 3. Validate the previous accepted state receipt and passive-chassis reference packet. Both must precede the current cycle and derive only from committed archive state. 4. Validate the phase packet, arousal scalar, destination policy, and immutable anchor-directory snapshot. 5. Compute raw and normalized keyframe novelty. 6. Compute cross-chassis cosine synchronization and transition-direction shear under explicit degeneracy policies. 7. Apply the first-match local outcome tree: FAULT, HOLD, CORPUS_MIGRATE_REPAIR_REQUEST, or ROUTE_INTENT_READY. 8. For ROUTE_INTENT_READY, quantize routing features, compute route-key and glyph digests, select one logical anchor deterministically, and derive temporal and phase-band metadata. 9. Seal output with every upstream digest, provider/profile identifier, policy epoch, and canonical serialization version.

SAME-CYCLE SNAPSHOT RULE Candidate, Sigma decision, phase packet, destination policy, and anchor-directory snapshot MUST identify the same route attempt. Previous accepted state and passive reference MUST be committed snapshots from cycles less than the current candidate cycle. Mixing active and passive data from different unbound epochs is a fault, not a repair condition.

4. Dual-Chassis Geometry and Readiness 4.1 Keyframe novelty Let X be the Sigma-authorized candidate and X_prev the newest committed predecessor. The raw delta is retained for diagnostics, while normalized novelty provides dimensionless comparison.

Page 7

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 8 / LORIEN Route-Intent and Indexing Contract

d = X - X_prev K_delta_raw = ||d||_2 K_delta = K_delta_raw / (||X||_2 + ||X_prev||_2 + epsilon_norm) 0 <= K_delta <= 1 The upper bound follows from the triangle inequality. K_delta_raw is scale-dependent; K_delta is the route-key feature. Neither value is a claim of semantic novelty or importance.

4.2 Cross-chassis synchronization Let C be the passive route-reference vector. Synchronization is the cosine similarity of the current state with that reference. tau_link = <X, C> / (||X||_2 * ||C||_2) The formula is evaluated only when both norms exceed epsilon_norm. A zero or near-zero reference produces HOLD_REFERENCE_DEGENERATE; it is not silently converted to a similarity of zero or one. sync_pass is true when tau_link >= tau_sync. Equality at 0.75 passes.

4.3 Transition-direction shear The source divided state variance by keyframe distance, which diverges for an unchanged state. The formal metric instead measures angular disagreement between the actual transition and the transition that would move from the predecessor toward the passive reference. d_ref = C - X_prev c_path = <d, d_ref> / (||d||_2 * ||d_ref||_2) S_shear = sqrt(max(0, (1 - clip(c_path, -1, 1)) / 2)) 0 <= S_shear <= 1       If ||d||_2 <= epsilon_norm, define S_shear = 0 and path_motion = false.       If path_motion is true but ||d_ref||_2 <= epsilon_norm, shear is not ready and the outcome is HOLD_PATH_REFERENCE_DEGENERATE.       Aligned motion gives 0, orthogonal motion gives sqrt(1/2), and directly reversed motion gives 1.       shear_pass is true when S_shear <= shear_max. Equality at 0.40 passes.

5. Logical Indexing, Memory Identity, and Anchor Selection 5.1 Quantized route features All route-key features use explicit integer quantization. The packet also retains the original float64 metrics for diagnostics. Quantization prevents platform-specific decimal formatting from changing the route key. phase_q = floor(wrap(phi_t, 2*pi) * phase_quantum_count / (2*pi)) novelty_q = round(K_delta * metric_quantum_count) sync_q = round(((tau_link + 1) / 2) * metric_quantum_count) shear_q = round(S_shear * metric_quantum_count) Each result is range-checked and serialized as an unsigned fixed-width integer in network byte order. The exact rounding mode is ties-to-even in the reference profile.

5.2 Route-key digest The route key distributes structurally related route intents without treating raw IEEE-754 bytes as public addresses. It binds policy and reference epochs so stale topology cannot be silently reused. route_key_digest = SHA256("LORIEN-RK1" || profile_id || session_id || cycle || structural_identity_digest || previous_state_digest || passive_reference_digest || destination_policy_digest || directory_digest || phase_q || novelty_q || sync_q || shear_q) The full candidate digest is carried separately in the RouteIntentPacket. The route key is not a security authorization and does not prove semantic equivalence.

5.3 Logical anchor slot anchor_slot = uint64_be(route_key_digest[0:8]) mod anchor_slot_count For the reference anchor_slot_count=16, modulo reduction is unbiased because 16 divides 2^64. For another slot count, the profile MUST use rejection sampling or document the exact finite bias.

5.4 Deterministic anchor selection Eligible anchors are UP, support the requested service and route class, and satisfy the destination allow-list. Prefer anchors in anchor_slot. If that set is empty, a policy-controlled all-slot fallback may be used and MUST set slot_fallback=true. score(anchor) = uint256(SHA256("LORIEN-HRW1" || route_key_digest || anchor_id)) / policy_weight(anchor) Select the anchor with maximum score; break an exact score tie by lexicographically smallest canonical anchor_id. This highest-random-weight selection is deterministic and avoids dependence on directory ordering. It selects a logical AnchorID only; Module 4 resolves that anchor into a node and path.

5.5 Memory identity and compact labels glyph_digest = SHA256("LORIEN-GLYPH1" || candidate_digest || structural_identity_digest || session_id || cycle) glyph_label32 = uint32_be(glyph_digest[0:4])    glyph_digest is the authoritative LORIEN memory/routing identity.    glyph_label32 is a compact collision-prone label for caches and frames; it is not unique.    Q and chi are carried unchanged from the structural-identity packet and remain authoritative for FBS branch identity.    A legacy Cantor32 label may be reported only when produced by a separately versioned integer quantizer. It is diagnostic and must never be used as an outer IPv4 destination.    RMX, not LORIEN, resolves persistent archive-address collisions.

6. Temporal Validity and Internal Phase-Band Metadata 6.1 Temporal-window policy The source policy is retained as an explicit piecewise configuration. “Arousal” is an internal scalar supplied by the EmotionTensor; the rule makes no clinical or psychological claim. m(a) = 0.5, when 0 <= a < 0.30 m(a) = 1.0, when 0.30 <= a <= 0.70 m(a) = 1.5, when 0.70 < a <= 1 T_res = round_half_even(T_base * m(a)) valid_from_cycle = cycle,    expires_at_cycle = cycle + T_res The intent is active when current_cycle < expires_at_cycle. It is expired at equality. Wall-clock timestamps may be logged but may not enter the deterministic intent digest.

6.2 Phase-band shift “Subnet Shift” is retained as an internal phase-band boundary flag, not an IPv4 subnet calculation. The phase provider supplies current_phase_band_id; the selected AnchorRecord supplies target_phase_band_id. phase_band_shift = (current_phase_band_id != target_phase_band_id) The output carries both identifiers and the provider/directory digests. No parity rule such as anchor_index mod 2 is normative because phase-band membership is a versioned policy attribute, not a property of an arbitrary numeric index.

7.2 RouteIntentPacket handoff        LOCAL_ARCHIVE and INTERNAL_DOMAIN intents may be handed directly to Module 4 after local authorization checks.        REMOTE_ALLOWED and REMOTE_REQUIRED intents MUST first be submitted to Guardian under REMOTE_EGRESS. Guardian verifies Sigma SEAL, payload identity, destination policy, and this LORIEN intent before it may issue PERMIT_GLYPHNET.        Module 4 validates the LORIEN intent digest and then performs internal directory resolution, QGM cost computation, path selection, framing, and local/internal/remote forwarding.        A RouteIntentPacket does not authorize archive commit, prove delivery, or create a persistent memory address.

7.3 LorienRepairRequest handoff A repair request includes the raw candidate, newest committed anchor, passive reference, synchronization and shear evidence, source Sigma decision, and no_commit=true. HARMONY decides whether its repair prerequisites are satisfied. LORIEN does not precompute Braidback weight and does not reuse a route intent after the candidate changes; a repaired candidate must pass downstream verification and receive a new Sigma/LORIEN attempt as specified by the orchestrator profile.

7.4 Hold semantics HOLD is neither rejection nor repair. It means LORIEN lacks a coherent snapshot or destination prerequisite. The exact candidate reference and every validated digest remain available to the caller. No exhaust mass, quarantine count, repair count, or FBS count is incremented merely because an intent is held.

7.5 Recovery boundary L_0=83 may be carried as inherited recovery metadata, but LORIEN never performs the FBS algorithm. A recovery request is restricted to catastrophic local control-state invariants, not to low sync, severe shear, missing anchors, expired windows, or Module 4 delivery failures.

8.4 Numerical conformance       Reference metric evaluation uses IEEE-754 binary64 with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.       Canonical serialization normalizes -0.0 to +0.0, rejects NaN and infinity, and uses network byte order.       Dot products and norms should use a deterministic reduction order or a declared backend tolerance profile.       Range clipping is permitted only for c_path and cosine values within numeric_tolerance of [-1,1]. Material range violations are faults.       Cross-backend conformance is tolerance-based for float diagnostics and byte-exact for canonical integer fields and digests after quantization.

X = input.candidate_state Xp = input.previous_accepted.state C = input.passive_reference.reference_vector

d = X - Xp k_raw = l2(d) k_norm = k_raw / (l2(X) + l2(Xp) + cfg.epsilon_norm)

if l2(X) <= eps or l2(C) <= eps: return hold(REFERENCE_DEGENERATE) tau_link = dot(X, C) / (l2(X) * l2(C))

if k_raw <= eps: shear = 0.0 else: d_ref = C - Xp if l2(d_ref) <= eps: return hold(PATH_REFERENCE_DEGENERATE) c_path = clip(dot(d, d_ref) / (l2(d) * l2(d_ref)), -1, 1) shear = sqrt(max(0, (1 - c_path) / 2))

if shear > cfg.shear_max: return repair_request(SEVERE_TRANSITION_SHEAR, tau_link, shear, no_commit=true) if tau_link < cfg.tau_sync: return repair_request(LOW_CHASSIS_SYNC, tau_link, shear, no_commit=true)

T_res = temporal_window(input.arousal, cfg) features = quantize(input.phase, k_norm, tau_link, shear, cfg) route_key = sha256(canonical_route_key(input, features))

It measures the crossing; it does not become the road. NORMATIVE STATUS This module is exact within its declared computational scope. HARMONY consumes one authorized repair request, one immutable candidate, one immutable repair target, one versioned thread-evidence packet, and one read-only Emotion Tensor snapshot. It computes a bounded repair severity, bounded thread-stability score, internal modulation gain, requested anchor weight, effective anchor fraction, and one convex repaired candidate. It emits one sealed repair packet, bounded-limit packet, hold, fault, or catastrophic recovery request. It does not accept a state, commit memory, create a route, mutate the archive, quarantine a glyph, debit or credit RTSOM, or execute FBS.

CLAIM BOUNDARY “Harmony,” “emotion,” “truth,” “Ego,” “Logos,” “thread,” and “Braidback” are architectural labels. Arousal is a bounded internal control scalar supplied by an upstream packet; HARMONY does not infer, diagnose, or judge a person’s emotions. “Truth 51% / correction 49%” means only that the raw candidate coefficient remains at least 0.51 while the selected repair-target coefficient remains at most 0.49. Effective-resistance and Hodge terminology are design analogies unless a separately versioned provider supplies those exact computations.

The module exists to attempt salvage without granting repair authority enough weight to overwrite the candidate lineage.

2. Architecture Role, Operating Profiles, and Lifecycle 2.1 Operating profiles Profile                       Authorized source              Repair target                     Base severity evidence

SigmaDecisionPacket            Newest committed accepted SIGMA_BRAIDBACK                                                                                RMF deficit below tau_eff route=BRAIDBACK_REQUEST        anchor

The request declares exactly one target. HARMONY never chooses among multiple targets and never searches the archive. A deployment may restrict LORIEN_REALIGN to committed anchors; the chosen target policy is versioned in HarmonyConfig.

2.2 Lifecycle states State                                                        Meaning

IDLE                                                         No active attempt.

Configuration, source request, candidate, target, thread VALIDATING evidence, and emotion packet are checked.

Severity, stability, modulation, and requested coefficient are MEASURING computed.

Repair would exceed policy or have no measurable effect; no LIMITED candidate revision is emitted.

REPAIRING                                                    One convex combination is computed in a private work buffer.

Coefficient, segment, digest, and numerical invariants are RECONCILING checked.

SEALED                                                       Exactly one immutable output packet is emitted.

FAULTED                                                      Typed fault emitted; inputs unchanged.

2.3 Required execution order 1. Validate HarmonyConfig against BootPacket, DIM, numeric profile, and schema versions. 2. Validate exactly one authorized source request and bind it to the candidate digest, session, cycle, lineage, and repair depth. 3. Validate the immutable repair target and its provenance. The target must precede or be independently derived without the current candidate. 4. Validate ThreadEvidencePacket and EmotionTensorSnapshot against the same candidate and cycle. 5. Compute source-specific normalized repair severity. 6. Compute bounded thread stability and thread factor. 7. Compute arousal modulation gain, requested weight, cap status, and effective anchor fraction. 8. Apply the first-match outcome tree: FAULT, HOLD, LIMIT, REPAIR, or catastrophic request. 9. For REPAIR, compute one convex candidate in a private buffer and reconcile every coefficient and digest. 10. Seal exactly one output. Clear all temporary buffers whether success or failure.

2.4 Attempt and re-entry rule The reference profile sets max_repair_depth=1. A HarmonyRepairPacket creates a new candidate revision. The source Sigma decision and any LORIEN route intent are no longer valid for the changed vector. Module 10 must audit the

repair first; after a SAFE audit, the hardened profile requires a new Sigma evaluation and, when routing is required, a new LORIEN attempt. HARMONY does not loop back into itself on the same source lineage.

4. Input Validation, Snapshot Consistency, and Canonicalization 4.1 Snapshot consistency       Every packet must share session_id, candidate_digest, cycle, profile lineage, and DIM.       The source request must be valid for the exact candidate and must not already be consumed.       The target is immutable during the attempt and may not be silently replaced after weight computation.       A committed target must precede the candidate cycle. A passive reference must prove candidate exclusion.       Thread and emotion evidence must be generated for the same candidate revision.       Repair depth, attempt identity, and lineage must prevent replay as a second repair of the same revision.

4.2 Numeric-domain validation       Candidate and target are exact-length float64 arrays with finite values in [-1,1]. Inputs outside this domain are faults; HARMONY does not clip them.       Arousal is finite and in [0,1]. Thread scores are finite and in [-1,1].       All thresholds and observed metrics must satisfy their declared domains before any division.       The candidate-target span must exceed epsilon_norm before a nonzero repair can be defined.       NaN, infinity, signed-zero distinctions, and subnormal policy are governed by numeric_profile_id and logged in conformance metadata.

4.3 Source predicate validation HARMONY does not re-run Sigma or LORIEN, but it verifies that the request is internally consistent with its declared route. A Sigma request must satisfy rmf_observed < tau_eff. A LORIEN request must satisfy tau_link < tau_sync or S_shear > S_shear_max. A mismatched predicate is a fault, not an invitation to reinterpret the route.

4.4 Canonicalization and hashing       Strings are UTF-8 with explicit lengths; integers are big-endian; arrays store declared length followed by IEEE-754 binary64 values in index order.       No wall-clock timestamp, object address, map iteration order, locale-formatted number, or platform path enters a deterministic digest.       Input digests are recomputed before use. Output is serialized once, hashed, read back, and re-hashed before SEALED.       Bitwise replay is required only within the same numeric_profile_id. Cross-backend conformance uses declared numerical tolerances and must not pretend that floating-point libraries are universally bit-identical.

5. Formal Repair Mechanics 5.1 Source-specific normalized severity The base severity d_base is a bounded control quantity in [0,1]. It measures distance beyond the source owner’s recoverable boundary; it is not a probability and does not prove semantic error.

5.1.1 Sigma Braidback severity d_sigma = clip((tau_eff - RMF_fail) / tau_eff, 0, 1) tau_eff must be positive. This retains the source deficit ratio while adding explicit clipping and domain validation. A reason_code of VARIANCE_RECONSTRUCT_FAIL may set d_base=max(d_sigma, d_cvc_provider) only when a separately versioned Sigma request supplies a bounded d_cvc_provider; HARMONY never reconstructs CVC itself.

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 9 / HARMONY Bounded Repair Contract

5.1.2 LORIEN realignment severity d_sync = clip((tau_sync - tau_link) / (tau_sync + 1), 0, 1) d_shear = clip((S_shear - S_shear_max) / (1 - S_shear_max), 0, 1) d_lorien = max(d_sync, d_shear) The denominators normalize each metric over its declared remaining domain. HARMONY uses the values sealed by LORIEN and does not recompute chassis geometry. d_base = d_sigma for SIGMA_BRAIDBACK;              d_base = d_lorien for LORIEN_REALIGN

5.2 Bounded thread stability The source ratio mean/std is unbounded and becomes artificially enormous when variance approaches zero. The formal profile first maps each mini-RMF score into [0,1], then uses a bounded mean-to-dispersion ratio. q_j = (c_j + 1) / 2,   j = 1,...,m mu_q = (1/m) * sum(q_j) sigma_q = sqrt((1/m) * sum((q_j - mu_q)^2)) H_s = 0, if mu_q = 0 and sigma_q = 0; otherwise H_s = mu_q / (mu_q + sigma_q) Therefore H_s is in [0,1]. The population standard deviation is used because C is the complete declared active-thread set for the attempt, not a statistical sample from an unobserved population. m_thread = 1.20, if H_s < 0.75; otherwise m_thread = 1.00 The 1.20 multiplier and 0.75 boundary preserve the source tuning while making the stability score’s domain exact.

5.3 Internal arousal modulation g_a = 1 - a,   with a in [0,1] g_a is the source-compatible anchor-gain multiplier. High internal arousal reduces how strongly HARMONY may pull toward the target; low arousal permits the full requested pull. The name “emotional frequency modulation” is an architectural analogy. No human emotional state is inferred.

5.4 Requested weight, cap, and effective anchor fraction w_requested = d_base * m_thread w_braid = min(w_requested, B_WEIGHT_MAX) alpha = w_braid * g_a w_requested is the unbounded-by-policy request, w_braid is the capped policy weight, and alpha is the coefficient actually applied to the repair target. Separating these values resolves the source ambiguity in which the reported Braidback weight and the actual interpolation coefficient were not the same.

51/49 INVARIANT A repair is emitted only when w_requested <= 0.49 and alpha > epsilon_norm. Since 0 <= g_a <= 1, alpha <= w_braid <= 0.49. The repaired candidate therefore retains coefficient 1-alpha >= 0.51 from the raw candidate and receives at most 0.49 from the declared repair target.

5.5 Bounded-limit conditions Condition                               Limit reason                                Meaning

The source deficit plus thread factor w_requested > 0.49                      REQUIRED_WEIGHT_EXCEEDS_CAP                 demands more authority than policy permits.

A lawful nonzero repair cannot be alpha <= epsilon_norm                   MODULATION_SUPPRESSED_REPAIR produced under the current modulation.

Page 9

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 9 / HARMONY Bounded Repair Contract

Condition                                 Limit reason                               Meaning

The target provides no distinct repair ||target-candidate|| <= epsilon_norm      DEGENERATE_REPAIR_SPAN                     direction; treated as an input inconsistency.

A limit is a bounded refusal, not deletion, quarantine, exhaust transfer, or FBS. The exact candidate and evidence remain available to the orchestrator.

5.6 Convex repair X_harm = (1 - alpha) * X_raw + alpha * X_target The operation is performed componentwise in one declared arithmetic order. Because both endpoints lie in [-1,1] and alpha is in [0,1], every output component remains in [-1,1] without clipping. The result lies on the closed line segment between candidate and target; it is not a projection onto an independently established manifold.

5.7 Empirical coefficient and reconciliation span_norm = ||X_target - X_raw||_2 repair_norm = ||X_harm - X_raw||_2 alpha_eff = repair_norm / span_norm convex_residual = ||X_harm - ((1-alpha)X_raw + alpha X_target)||_2 For a nondegenerate span, alpha_eff must agree with alpha within reconcile_tolerance. Module 10 independently recomputes alpha_eff from the three vectors rather than trusting HARMONY’s reported values.

5.8 Diagnostic alignment measurements A_before = cosine(X_raw, X_target) A_after = cosine(X_harm, X_target) Delta_A = A_after - A_before These are diagnostics only. HARMONY does not declare the repair coherent, safe, or accepted based on Delta_A. Zero- vector policies are explicit: a zero candidate or target is a fault under the reference profile.

5.9 Deterministic repair identity and IMM_ID repair_digest = SHA256("SC-HARMONY-REPAIR-1" || source_request_digest || candidate_digest || target_digest || thread_digest || emotion_digest || config_digest || canonical_metrics || repaired_digest) IMM_ID = "HARM-" || first_24_hex(repair_digest) repair_digest is authoritative. IMM_ID is a compact display and pathway token and is not assumed globally collision- free. The source timestamp-based identifier is removed because wall time breaks deterministic replay.

5.10 Complexity For dimension D and m thread scores, time complexity is Theta(D+m) and auxiliary working memory is Theta(D+m) when the repaired vector is materialized. It is not O(1) with respect to DIM.

6.2 Mandatory Module 10 audit         Every HarmonyRepairPacket is submitted to Module 10 before any SERAPHIM, route, or archive action.         Module 10 recomputes alpha_eff from X_raw, X_target, and X_harm; verifies the 0.49 limit; and performs its separately defined nested-harm scan.         HARMONY cannot mark its own output SAFE and cannot convert a Module 10 rejection into an alternate local route.

6.3 Revalidation after mutation A repaired candidate is a new revision with a new digest. Any Sigma decision or LORIEN intent bound to X_raw is invalid for X_harm. The hardened reference profile requires: Module 10 SAFE -> new Sigma evaluation -> new LORIEN intent when routing is required -> downstream validation. The source-compatible direct Module 10 -> SERAPHIM path may be implemented only as an explicitly different integration profile and must not reuse stale Sigma/LORIEN authorizations.

6.4 Limit and hold semantics LIMIT means policy denied the requested degree of correction or modulation produced no effective repair. HOLD means a required provider snapshot is not ready. Neither result changes the candidate, counts as quarantine, creates exhaust mass, or proves that the branch is irrecoverable. A later attempt requires a new authorized request or newly versioned evidence; it may not silently reuse a consumed attempt ID.

6.5 Recovery boundary L_0=83 may be carried in inherited FBS metadata, but HARMONY does not diagonalize history, perform a Collatz fold, produce a new seed, or write the exhaust budget. An ordinary weight-cap breach, low thread stability, high arousal, failed downstream audit, or repeated coherence failure is not by itself a catastrophic local invariant.

10. Property, Fuzz, Concurrency, and Stress Testing 10.1 Property tests         Convexity: for random valid endpoints and alpha in [0,0.49], every output component lies between endpoint components.         Coefficient identity: alpha_eff equals alpha within tolerance for every nondegenerate endpoint pair.         Authority bound: target coefficient never exceeds 0.49 and raw coefficient never falls below 0.51.         Endpoint behavior: alpha=0 returns raw exactly; alpha approaching 0.49 remains inside the segment.         Monotonic modulation: with fixed request and evidence, increasing arousal never increases alpha.         Thread-factor bound: m_thread is exactly 1 or 1.20 and cannot exceed the configured maximum.         No mutation: hashes of all input packets are unchanged after every outcome.

10.2 Fuzz tests    Malformed lengths, duplicate fields, invalid enums, noncanonical NaNs, infinities, signed zeros, subnormals, and hash truncation.    Boundary values around 0.49, 0.75, 1.20, arousal 0/1, tau thresholds, and epsilon_norm.    Candidate/target arrays at DIM-1, DIM, and DIM+1.    Digest swaps among candidate, target, thread, emotion, Sigma, and LORIEN packets.    Adversarial target vectors designed to maximize cancellation and floating-point error.

10.3 Concurrency tests    Two workers processing the same attempt must converge on one idempotent sealed output.    A late target-provider update may not alter an in-flight attempt’s immutable snapshot.    A replay arriving after SEALED returns the prior result or H_REPLAY according to orchestrator policy; it never performs a second repair.    A target or thread digest conflict is isolated to the attempt and cannot mutate shared provider state.

10.4 Stress profile Execute at least 100,000 attempts across both source profiles, randomized valid vectors, all boundary conditions, and mixed outcomes. Verify counter reconciliation, zero leaked work buffers, bounded memory growth, no direct destination-owner mutation, and no FBS request outside the five enumerated catastrophic conditions.

11. Reference Pseudocode def harmony_attempt(inp: HarmonyInput, cfg: HarmonyConfig): validate_config(cfg, inp.boot_digest) validate_snapshot_bindings(inp, cfg)

if inp.thread_evidence.status == NOT_READY: return seal_hold(reason="THREAD_EVIDENCE_NOT_READY", no_commit=True)

validate_candidate(inp.candidate, cfg.DIM) validate_target(inp.repair_target, inp.candidate_digest, inp.cycle, cfg) validate_threads(inp.thread_evidence, inp.candidate_digest, cfg) validate_emotion(inp.emotion, inp.candidate_digest) validate_source_predicate(inp.source_request)

if inp.source_request.kind == SIGMA_BRAIDBACK: d_base = clip( (inp.source_request.tau_eff - inp.source_request.rmf_observed) / inp.source_request.tau_eff, 0.0, 1.0) else: d_sync = clip( (inp.source_request.tau_sync - inp.source_request.tau_link) / (inp.source_request.tau_sync + 1.0), 0.0, 1.0) d_shear = clip( (inp.source_request.s_shear - inp.source_request.s_shear_max) / (1.0 - inp.source_request.s_shear_max), 0.0, 1.0) d_base = max(d_sync, d_shear)

q = [(c + 1.0) / 2.0 for c in inp.thread_evidence.scores] mu_q = mean(q) sigma_q = population_std(q) H_s = 0.0 if mu_q == 0.0 and sigma_q == 0.0 else mu_q / (mu_q + sigma_q) thread_factor = cfg.thread_factor_low if H_s < cfg.h_s_threshold else 1.0

arousal_gain = 1.0 - inp.emotion.arousal w_requested = d_base * thread_factor w_braid = min(w_requested, cfg.b_weight_max)

span = inp.repair_target.vector - inp.candidate if norm2(span) <= cfg.epsilon_norm: raise HarmonyFault("H_TARGET_DEGENERATE")

2.3 Required execution order 1. Validate Module10Config against BootPacket, DIM, numeric profile, schema, canonical encoding, and hash profile. 2. Accept exactly one authorized source profile and freeze all source bytes and digests. 3. Validate session, cycle, candidate revision, parent lineage, source owner, and one-time attempt identifier. 4. Validate candidate shape, finite domain, declared digest, capability descriptor, and prior authorization invalidation state. 5. For HARMONY_REPAIR, independently recompute the repair coefficient and segment residuals. 6. Validate HarmFeaturePacket provider identity, candidate binding, feature registry, hard-flag types, and evidence digests. 7. Compute the exact hard-flag total zeta_hard and diagnostics. 8. Apply the first-match outcome tree: catastrophic request, fault, hold, quarantine request, or SAFE eligibility. 9. Canonicalize and seal exactly one result. On quarantine, retain the exact source reference until a matching custody receipt or backpressure outcome exists.

2.4 Mutation and re-entry rule Module 10 never changes the candidate. A SAFE audit does not restore authorizations that were bound to a prior candidate digest. For a HARMONY repair, the hardened sequence is Module 10 SAFE -> new Sigma evaluation -> new LORIEN intent when required -> Module 11. For an RMX synthesis, the orchestration layer uses an RMX revalidation token bound to the paused Psi transaction; after required validation, Psi resumes with the same immutable RMX resolution and must not rerun collision synthesis for that transaction.

4. Input Validation, Snapshot Consistency, and Canonicalization 4.1 Structural validation      All vectors have shape (DIM,), binary64 representation, finite values, and declared digest match.      Exactly one source profile is present. HARMONY and RMX fields may not be mixed in one attempt.      Source owner, schema version, session, cycle, lineage, candidate revision, and attempt id are mutually consistent.      The HarmFeaturePacket is bound to the same candidate digest and attempt id and uses the configured feature registry.      The active-lineage snapshot predates the audit decision and excludes future state.      Capability bits are explicit. Missing capability evidence is a fault, not an implicit pass.

4.2 Canonical serialization 1. Encode integers as signed or unsigned big-endian values with fixed width declared by schema. 2. Encode float64 values and arrays as IEEE-754 binary64 big-endian bytes in C order with shape metadata. 3. Encode strings as UTF-8 with explicit byte length. 4. Sort maps by UTF-8 key bytes; preserve list and feature-registry order. 5. Encode Booleans as one byte 0 or 1; reject noncanonical alternatives. 6. Hash source packet, candidate, lineage, capability descriptor, provider packet, quarantine policy, computed metrics, and decision into audit_digest.

4.3 Snapshot consistency The audit uses frozen snapshots. Provider version, feature registry, lineage history, quarantine policy, and numeric profile may not change during an attempt. A new version applies only to a new attempt. Two contents claiming the same authoritative version and epoch with different digests constitute a catastrophic policy split.

4.4 Determinism boundary The reference profile guarantees deterministic output bytes only within one declared numeric backend profile. Cross- platform conformance is tolerance-based for recomputed floating-point diagnostics and byte-exact for canonical source arrays and sealed packet fields after canonicalization.

5. Braidback Empirical Audit 5.1 Source formula defect and correction The source formula used the distance from the repaired point to the anchor in the numerator. For a lawful interpolation X_harm=(1-alpha)X_raw+alpha X_target, that ratio evaluates approximately to 1-alpha, inverting the intended repair weight. Module 10 therefore audits displacement from the raw candidate toward the target, plus an independent collinearity residual.

5.2 Definitions s = X_target - X_raw d = X_harm - X_raw span2 = <s,s> If sqrt(span2) <= epsilon_norm, emit M10_REPAIR_SPAN. No ratio is evaluated. alpha_proj = <d,s> / span2 Signed barycentric coefficient along the declared repair segment. alpha_dist = ||d||_2 / ||s||_2 Independent displacement-magnitude ratio. r_orth = ||d - alpha_proj*s||_2 / ||s||_2 Normalized off-segment residual. r_model = ||X_harm - ((1-alpha_reported)X_raw + alpha_reported X_target)||_2 / ||s||_2

5.3 Pass predicate Check                                                            Reference predicate

Finite metrics                                                   alpha_proj, alpha_dist, r_orth, and r_model are finite.

Direction                                                        alpha_proj >= -coefficient_tolerance.

51/49 authority                                                  alpha_proj <= 0.49 + coefficient_tolerance.

Raw majority                                                     1-alpha_proj >= 0.51 - coefficient_tolerance.

Reported coefficient                                             |alpha_proj-alpha_reported| <= coefficient_tolerance.

Distance coefficient                                             |alpha_dist-alpha_proj| <= coefficient_tolerance.

Segment membership                                               r_orth <= segment_tolerance.

Model reconciliation                                             r_model <= segment_tolerance.

Every X_harm component is within endpoint bounds plus Component bounds tolerance.

Digest identity                                                  All three vector digests match the HarmonyRepairPacket.

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 10 / Braidback Audit and IMMUNE_SYSTEM

51/49 INVARIANT For a passed HARMONY_REPAIR audit, alpha_eff := alpha_proj lies in [0,0.49] within declared tolerance, the orthogonal residual is negligible, and X_harm lies on the endpoint segment. The raw-candidate coefficient is therefore at least 0.51. This is a coefficient and lineage policy only; it is not a statement about factual truth, ego, morality, or human judgment.

5.4 Boundary behavior       alpha_proj=0.49 exactly passes when all residual checks pass.       A negative coefficient is extrapolation away from the target and fails.       A coefficient above 1 is extrapolation beyond the target and fails before the 0.49 check.       An off-line point with the correct displacement norm fails r_orth.       A packet reporting alpha=0.20 while the vectors encode alpha=0.30 fails reconciliation.       Rounding within configured tolerance is reported explicitly and does not change the stored source arrays.

5.5 RMX profile The 51/49 audit is NOT_APPLICABLE for RMX_SYNTHESIS because the source does not define a single raw-target convex segment. Module 10 must not invent one. The audit packet records the weight-audit status as NOT_APPLICABLE and instead validates the RMX resolution identity, all parent state digests, synthesis provenance, final address binding, and paused-transaction token.

6.2 Nested-harm metric zeta_hard(G) = sum_i phi_i(G), phi_i in {0,1} SAFE evidence condition: zeta_hard(G) <= tau_harm = 0 The strict source value tau_harm=0 is retained as zero allowed hard flags. Soft scores are diagnostic telemetry only in the reference profile. A provider may promote a diagnostic to a hard flag only through a new feature-registry version and conformance set.

6.3 Contextual arousal The source “peak arousal > 1.5” signature is incompatible with the architecture’s normalized arousal domain [0,1]. It is removed as a hard harm signal. Arousal may be carried as bounded context telemetry, but arousal alone cannot produce a hard flag, quarantine, or claim of panic.

6.4 Replay and non-progress The source compared two vector halves, which is undefined for odd DIM=81 and confuses spatial repetition with recursive non-progress. The reference profile uses exact digest and progress-token history instead. Optional periodicity diagnostics may be computed without affecting the route: r_p = ||X[p:] - X[:-p]||_2 / (||X[p:]||_2 + ||X[:-p]||_2 + epsilon_norm) For each configured p<DIM, r_p is logged. A low r_p is a periodicity observation, not a harm verdict. Exact replay becomes a hard flag only when the lineage lacks authorized reuse.

6.5 Morse and persistence provider boundary        A provider invoking Discrete Morse analysis must define the finite cell/simplicial complex, scalar field, adjacency, boundary convention, critical-cell tie-break, and threshold.        A provider invoking parameterized persistence must define the filtration family, parameter domain/grid, coefficient field, stability tolerance, barcode/canopy summary, and decision rule.        “Critical elements exceed expected limits” is not executable and is rejected unless the expected limit and exact count procedure are in the provider configuration.        The provider packet is evidence. Module 10 validates and aggregates it; it does not silently substitute a different topology algorithm.

11. Property, Fuzz, Concurrency, and Stress Testing 11.1 Property tests         For random X_raw, X_target, and alpha in [0,0.49], exact interpolation yields alpha_proj approximately alpha and r_orth approximately zero.         For any nonzero orthogonal perturbation above tolerance, the segment audit rejects even when alpha_dist remains below 0.49.         zeta_hard equals the population count of true registered hard flags and is independent of map insertion order.         No accepted input produces a SAFE packet carrying execute, route, archive-commit, or egress capability.         Canonical reserialization is idempotent and preserves audit_digest.

11.2 Metamorphic tests         Applying the same positive scalar to raw, target, and repaired vectors leaves alpha_proj and normalized residuals unchanged, subject to finite range.         Permuting vector coordinates identically across all three repair vectors leaves coefficient metrics unchanged.         Reordering hard-flag map insertion before canonical sorting leaves zeta_hard and audit_digest unchanged.         Changing a soft score while all hard flags remain false changes telemetry and packet digest but not the reference route.         Changing any source byte while preserving displayed decimal text changes the source digest and therefore the audit digest.

11.3 Fuzz and malformed-input tests         Fuzz packet lengths, UTF-8 strings, duplicate keys, integer widths, float payloads, array shapes, and digest fields.         Fuzz provider registries with unknown features, wrong types, duplicate names, missing evidence, and inconsistent method declarations.         Fuzz quarantine receipts, capability masks, attempt replays, RMX pause tokens, and source-profile confusion.         No malformed input may allocate an unbounded array, obtain SAFE eligibility, or mutate custody/archive state.

11.4 Concurrency and crash tests         Two workers auditing the same attempt id must converge on one sealed result; the loser receives the idempotent result or a replay fault.         Provider and policy epoch swaps during evaluation do not affect the frozen attempt.         A crash after QuarantineRequest but before receipt leaves one pending exact object reference and no false acknowledgement.

Page 18

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 10 / Braidback Audit and IMMUNE_SYSTEM

   A crash after SAFE seal preserves the audit packet but does not imply downstream revalidation occurred.

11.5 Stress requirements    Run at least 100,000 mixed repair and RMX audits across provider and policy versions.    Reconcile all outcome, custody, revalidation, and recovery counters exactly.    Bound memory used for lineage history, provider evidence indexes, and pending custody references.    Compare at least two permitted numerical backends using tolerance-based metric parity and canonical packet verification.

12. Reference Pseudocode def module10_audit(inp, cfg, registry, journal, custody): freeze = canonical_freeze(inp, cfg) validate_config(cfg, freeze.boot) validate_source_union(freeze) validate_lineage_capabilities_and_digests(freeze)

prior = journal.lookup(freeze.attempt_id) if prior is not None: return prior # exact idempotent result

if catastrophic_precondition(freeze): return seal_fbs_request(freeze)

if freeze.features.status == NOT_READY: return seal_hold(freeze, dependency="HarmFeatureProvider") if freeze.features.status == FAULT: return seal_fault(freeze, "M10_PROVIDER_FAULT")

hard_flags = ordered_registered_flags(freeze.features, registry)

if freeze.profile == HARMONY_REPAIR: s = freeze.x_target - freeze.x_raw d = freeze.x_candidate - freeze.x_raw span = norm2(s) if span <= cfg.epsilon_norm: return seal_fault(freeze, "M10_REPAIR_SPAN")

alpha_proj = dot(d, s) / dot(s, s) alpha_dist = norm2(d) / span r_orth = norm2(d - alpha_proj * s) / span model = (1.0 - freeze.alpha_reported) * freeze.x_raw                   + freeze.alpha_reported * freeze.x_target r_model = norm2(freeze.x_candidate - model) / span

weight_ok = ( finite(alpha_proj, alpha_dist, r_orth, r_model) and alpha_proj >= -cfg.coefficient_tolerance and alpha_proj <= cfg.b_weight_max + cfg.coefficient_tolerance and abs(alpha_proj - freeze.alpha_reported) <= cfg.coefficient_tolerance and abs(alpha_dist - alpha_proj) <= cfg.coefficient_tolerance and r_orth <= cfg.segment_tolerance and r_model <= cfg.segment_tolerance and componentwise_between(freeze.x_candidate, freeze.x_raw, freeze.x_target, cfg.segment_tolerance) ) hard_flags["REPAIR_WEIGHT_BREACH"] = not weight_ok weight_metrics = seal_weight_metrics(...) else: validate_rmx_binding(freeze) weight_metrics = NOT_APPLICABLE

hard_flags["UNAUTHORIZED_REPLAY"] = unauthorized_replay(freeze, cfg) hard_flags["NONPROGRESSIVE_CYCLE"] = nonprogress(freeze, cfg) hard_flags["UNAUTHORIZED_CAPABILITY"] = any_forbidden_capability(freeze)

Page 19

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 10 / Braidback Audit and IMMUNE_SYSTEM

hard_flags["LINEAGE_BREAK"] = lineage_break(freeze)

zeta_hard = sum(1 for value in hard_flags.values() if value)

if zeta_hard > cfg.tau_harm: decision = seal_quarantine_request(freeze, hard_flags, weight_metrics, zeta_hard) journal.commit_once(decision) return decision

decision = seal_safe_audit(freeze, hard_flags, weight_metrics, zeta_hard, next_step_token(freeze)) journal.commit_once(decision) return decision
