13. Property, Metamorphic, Fuzz, Concurrency, and Stress Testing 13.1 Property tests       Generate random finite vectors and angles; verify pairwise phase correction preserves L2 norm within backend tolerance.       Verify every reference reconstruction has DIM entries and every feature count matches its view profile.       Verify score=min(coherence,fidelity), eligibility is monotone in the configured threshold, and selection is the exact minimum under the tie-break order.       Verify load, M_t, R_t, HOT, and quadrature energy bounds for randomized inputs.       Verify canonical serialization is stable across process restart, dictionary order, thread schedule, and platform endianness.

13.2 Metamorphic tests       Multiply state and baseline by the same positive scalar: cosine gates and normalized M_t remain invariant within tolerance.       Add a full 2pi multiple to theta: phase-corrected and render bytes remain identical after canonical wrapping.       Reorder provider result delivery: the selected view and scan digest remain unchanged.       Change H_G while all presentation inputs remain fixed: POST_COMMIT_SCAN output remains unchanged.       Increase only a candidate cost while keeping metrics fixed: selection may move only according to the deterministic cost order.

13.3 Fuzz and adversarial tests       Fuzz packet lengths, shapes, float encodings, NaN payloads, huge norms, signed zero, subnormals, and malformed digests.       Fuzz provider IDs, representation shapes, duplicate view IDs, negative costs, and non-canonical orderings.       Fuzz permit expiry, duplicate receipts, target substitution, branch substitution, and incident sequence replay.       Attempt to smuggle executable instructions or external-routing capabilities into render metadata; reject by schema.

13.4 Concurrency and crash recovery       Run concurrent identical scans: deduplicate by attempt key or produce byte-identical packets; never two conflicting permits.       Run two UI consumers against one permit: at most one valid consumption transition.       Crash after render sealing but before permit publication: no consumed permit exists after recovery.       Crash after UI receipt journal write but before counter update: replay reconciles exactly once.       Run concurrent recovery watches for one incident: at most one valid FBS activation permit. A persisted journal is required for every permit and receipt transition; in-memory counters are never authoritative after a crash.

Page 21

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 15 / ROVER Presentation and Recovery Watchdog

13.5 Stress and backend parity    Execute at least 100,000 POST_COMMIT_SCAN attempts across threshold-adjacent vectors and verify zero nondeterministic output drift.    Execute at least 100,000 phase rotations and track maximum norm error.    Sustain repeated UI expiry and retry without permit leakage or archive mutation.    Partition and rejoin the presentation receipt journal; reject conflicting consumption histories.    Compare approved numerical backends on a locked corpus; threshold decisions must agree and byte differences must follow the declared backend profile.

14. Reference Pseudocode def rover_post_commit_scan(inp: RoverScanInput, cfg: RoverConfig): validate_config(cfg) frozen = validate_and_freeze(inp)

e = canonical_float64(frozen.commit.state_vector) b = canonical_float64(frozen.baseline.baseline_vector) e_prime = pair_rotate(e, frozen.observer.theta) assert_close(norm2(e_prime), norm2(e), cfg.numeric_tolerance)

candidates = [] for profile in frozen.projection_profiles_sorted: p_e = profile.project(e_prime) p_b = profile.project(b) recon = profile.reconstruct(p_e) coherence = cosine_with_policy(p_e, p_b, kind="coherence") fidelity = cosine_with_policy(e_prime, recon, kind="fidelity") score = min(coherence.value, fidelity.value) candidates.append(seal_candidate(profile, p_e, p_b, recon, coherence, fidelity, score))

eligible = [c for c in candidates if c.readiness == READY and c.coherence >= cfg.tau_view and c.fidelity >= cfg.tau_view] if not eligible: return RoverHoldPacket(reason="NO_COHERENT_VIEW", no_mutation=True)

selected = min(eligible, key=lambda c: (c.cost_units, c.nominal_dimension, c.view_id, c.candidate_digest))

delta_tau = logical_pacing(e_prime, inp.delta_cycle, cfg) stability = bounded_stability(e_prime, b, cfg) trend = comparable_trend(selected, inp.previous_scan, delta_tau, cfg) hot = bounded_hot(selected.score, stability, trend, cfg)

scan = seal_scan_packet(frozen, e_prime, candidates, selected, delta_tau, stability, trend, hot) if hot < cfg.hot_threshold: return RoverHoldPacket(reason="HOT_LOCK", scan_digest=scan.digest, no_mutation=True)

render = quadrature_render(selected.features, frozen.observer.theta, frozen.observer.omega, inp.delta_cycle) permit = issue_single_use_permit(render, scan, ttl_cycles=1) return scan, render, permit

def rover_recovery_watch(inp: RecoveryWatchInput, cfg: RoverConfig): incident = validate_catastrophic_incident(inp.incident) lock_broadcast(incident.branch_digest) watch_scan = compute_incident_bound_hot(inp, cfg)

if watch_scan.hot >= cfg.hot_threshold: return RoverHoldPacket(reason="RECOVERY_NOT_CONFIRMED", no_mutation=True)

return issue_fbs_activation_permit( incident_digest=incident.digest, branch_digest=incident.branch_digest, authorized_executor="MODULE16_FBS", authorized_actions=["ROLLBACK", "FBS_GEOMETRY", "DIAGONALIZE", "COLLATZ_FOLD", "RETURN_SEED"], no_rtsom_mutation_by_rover=True, )

1. Normative Scope, Statement Classes, and Non-Goals 1.1 Module purpose Module 16 is the owner of the FBS integer geometry and the terminal recovery execution procedure. Its geometry profile creates typed self-similar hierarchical blocks from declared modes and constructors. Its recovery profile validates an externally authorized incident, selects a reversible rollback target from immutable Psi checkpoints, and either emits a checkpoint-restore plan or derives a deterministic bounded reseed plan. Every output is digest-bound and non-mutating until the receiving owner acknowledges it.

CORE BOUNDARY FBS builds the structure and, when properly activated, computes the recovery plan. ROVER authorizes recovery. Psi supplies immutable checkpoints and remains archive owner. RTSOM accepts exact recovery residue. Delta consumes a published seed or restore plan. Phi records a completed recovery event. Equal H, Q, marked count, or inventory never authorizes substituting one constructor geometry for another.

Normative Directed and Bilateral Geometry 6.1 Admissible mode and directed atom M(tau,g), tau >= 2, 1 <= g < tau, delta = tau - g V+(tau,g) = (0, tau-g, tau, 2tau-g, 2tau, 3tau-g, 3tau, 3tau+1) L0 = 3tau + 2 The eight coordinates are strictly ordered. The terminal coordinate 3tau+1 is the directed binder, and the containing directed support is [0, L0-1]. For seed S, translate every coordinate by S.

6.2 Atomic bilateralization B(X) = X union (-X) W(tau,g) = B(V+(tau,g)) |W| = 15, R0 = 3tau+1, H0 = 6tau+3 = 2L0-1 Q0 = H0+2 = 2L0+1 = 6tau+5 Every atomic W is reflection-symmetric and its unweighted coordinate sum is zero. H0 is the inclusive span of the containing interval; it is not the number of marked coordinates.

Recursive Constructors, Identity Ladder, and Inverse Rules 7.1 Value equivalence and noncommutation H_parent = H1+H2+H3+4 Q_parent = Q1+Q2+Q3 For the same three directed children, G and C have equal inclusive span, marked count, leaf inventory, and Q. They generally do not have equal coordinates. For A,A,A, both have H=499, Q=501, and 49 marks; G contains coordinate 165 and excludes 140, while C contains 140 and excludes 165. The dense mode M(2,1) is a valid edge case where the two constructors coincide at the first homogeneous level.

NONCOMMUTATION RULE B(D(T1,T2,T3)) is not generally equal to C(B(T1),B(T2),B(T3)). The implementation must preserve the constructor tag and ordered tree. Equal scalar summaries never authorize a geometry substitution.

The centered marked density approaches 17/(6tau+5), a nonzero constant. The formal descriptor is self-similar hierarchical, not a claim of non- integer metric dimension.

7.4 Inverse and terminal-floor rules Directed homogeneous inverse: L_child = (L_parent-1)/3 Centered homogeneous inverse: H_child = (H_parent-4)/3 The inverse is defined only when the declared homogeneous constructor and divisibility conditions hold. Plain H/3 is nonconforming. For every atomic mode, L0 is congruent to 2 modulo 3 and H0-4 is congruent to 2 modulo 3, so the atom is not the homogeneous image of a smaller integer FBS object. Heterogeneous rollback must traverse the recorded ordered labeled tree. Scalar inversion is not permitted because Q and H do not preserve decomposition.

8. Recovery Activation and Transaction Protocol 8.1 Permit validation 1. Verify the permit issuer is Module 15 ROVER under the current trust configuration. 2. Verify permit_id has not been consumed, expired, revoked, or completed. 3. Verify incident_digest, affected branch, archive_head, policy_epoch, and requested recovery scope match the evidence bundle. 4. Verify the incident class is registered as catastrophic by the frozen recovery policy. 5. Atomically reserve the permit in the FBS recovery ledger using compare-and-swap. A duplicate request returns the prior result or current in-flight state.

8.2 Branch freeze and checkpoint validation 1. Require a BranchFreezeReceipt for the affected branch. ROVER broadcast lock alone does not prove the runtime stopped writes. 2. Verify the Psi checkpoint bundle is bound to the permit archive head and contains a continuous parent-digest chain. 3. Verify every checkpoint carries the exact constructor tag, ordered tree digest, mode metadata, geometry digest, and commit sequence required for reversal. 4. Reject or hold stale, incomplete, contradictory, unsigned, or post-incident checkpoints.

8.3 Deterministic rollback selection Select the newest checkpoint satisfying all of the following: committed before the incident boundary; declared known- good by the authorized source; digest-valid; not implicated by the incident; compatible with the frozen policy and constructor path. Ties are resolved by greatest committed sequence, then lexicographically smallest checkpoint ID.

Replays return the same receipt and never create a second event.

9. Bounded Diagonal Witness, Collatz Trace, and Seed Derivation 9.1 Finite diagonal witness Construct a canonical matrix from at most DIAGONAL_WIDTH authenticated evidence rows. Each row is a fixed-width bit string derived from a declared evidence digest. For n rows and width w with n <= w: d_i = 1 - M_i,i for 0 <= i < n The remaining bits are filled by a versioned digest-expansion rule, not by an unqualified constant pad. The resulting d differs from each examined row i at bit i. This is a local finite witness only. It does not prove global uniqueness, a new address, or freedom from collision outside the examined matrix.

9.2 Bounded Collatz trace C(n) = n/2 when n is even; C(n) = 3n+1 when n is odd Let n0 be a nonzero integer derived from the recovery material digest. Iterate only while step_count < COLLATZ_STEP_LIMIT and bit_length(n) <= COLLATZ_MAX_BITS. Stop with one of the exact statuses below.

Status                    Meaning

REACHED_ONE               n reached 1 within both limits

STEP_LIMIT                Configured step limit reached

BIT_LIMIT                 Configured intermediate integer bit length exceeded

Page 10

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 16 / FBS Geometry and Recovery Executor

Status                    Meaning

INVALID_INPUT             n0 was zero, negative, malformed, or inconsistent with the digest

A limited trace is a held recovery, not an infinite loop and not proof of mathematical failure. The module never assumes the Collatz conjecture.

9.3 Deterministic seed derivation escape_material = SHA256(canonical(permit, incident, floor tree, diagonal witness, policy epoch)) trace_digest = SHA256(canonical(n0, visited trace, status, step count, max bits)) S_next = 1 + (int(SHA256(escape_material || trace_digest), 16) mod (2^SEED_BITS - 1)) The seed is nonzero, deterministic, and bound to the full recovery transaction. It is not the terminal Collatz value 1 and is not claimed globally unique. Identical canonical incidents under the same policy reproduce the same seed; different bound evidence changes the derivation digest with cryptographic probability.

WHY THE SOURCE PROCEDURE CHANGED A finite diagonal flip guarantees difference only from the rows whose diagonal bits were examined. An unbounded Collatz-to-4-2-1 requirement depends on an unproved conjecture, and using the terminal value as the seed collapses every successful trace to the same integer. The hardened profile keeps both operations as bounded deterministic witnesses while deriving the actual seed from the complete authenticated trace.

10. Outcomes, Invariants, Faults, and Terminal Control Failures 10.1 Normative invariants I-01 Mode domain: tau >= 2 and 1 <= g < tau. I-02 Directed atom: V+ contains exactly eight distinct strictly ordered coordinates. I-03 Atomic bilateral: W=B(V+) contains exactly fifteen distinct coordinates and is reflection-symmetric. I-04 Exact scalar relations: L0=3tau+2, H0=6tau+3, Q0=6tau+5. I-05 Constructor tag: every recursive centered object is tagged GLOBAL_BILATERAL or LOCAL_CENTERED. I-06 Child order: ordered child identity is preserved even when Q and chi are accumulated. I-07 Q additivity: Q_parent=Q1+Q2+Q3 for both centered constructors. I-08 Identity separation: equal Q, H, marked count, or chi never implies coordinate equality. I-09 Symmetry by type: atomic and G require X=-X; heterogeneous C uses the local symmetry criterion. I-10 Inverse typing: scalar inverse is used only for a declared homogeneous constructor with exact divisibility. I-11 Heterogeneous reversal: exact rollback follows the ordered labeled tree. I-12 Capacity safety: exceeding a configured geometry cap produces HOLD and cannot self-authorize recovery. I-13 Recovery activation: RECOVERY_EXECUTE requires a current single-use Module 15 permit. I-14 Frozen evidence: permit, incident, policy, checkpoint bundle, and archive head remain immutable for one transaction. I-15 No source mutation: evaluation and plan construction do not mutate Psi, Delta, RTSOM, Phi, or caller state. I-16 Bounded integer processing: diagonal width, Collatz steps, and integer bit length are finite and enforced. I-17 Custody before completion: required RTSOM residue has a matching durable receipt before completion. I-18 Consumption before completion: Delta confirms exact plan/seed consumption before completion. I-19 Exactly once: one permit yields at most one committed recovery result and one Phi completion event. I-20 Determinism: identical canonical input and frozen policy yield byte-identical outputs and digests.

13. Reference Pseudocode and ASCII System Flow 13.1 Geometry pseudocode function build_geometry(req, registry, limits): freeze(req, registry, limits) mode = validate_mode(req.mode_id, req.tau, req.g) if predicted_size(req) > limits.capacity: return CapacityHold(no_mutation=true)

if req.tag == DIRECTED: object = directed_atom_or_parent(req) elif req.tag == ATOMIC_BILATERAL: object = bilateralize(directed_atom(mode)) elif req.tag == GLOBAL_BILATERAL: object = bilateralize(directed_parent(req.ordered_children)) elif req.tag == LOCAL_CENTERED: object = local_centered_parent(req.ordered_children) else: return Fault(FBS_CONSTRUCTOR_TAG)

derive L, H, Q, marked_count, binder_count, chi tree_digest = SHA256(canonical_ordered_tree) geometry_digest = SHA256(canonical(object, metadata)) assert type_specific_invariants(object) return GeometryPacket(no_mutation=true)

13.2 Recovery pseudocode function execute_recovery(permit, incident, checkpoints, freeze_receipt, policy): frozen = canonical_freeze(permit, incident, checkpoints, freeze_receipt, policy) verify_rover_permit(frozen) tx = reserve_permit_cas(permit.id) if tx.already_committed: return tx.committed_receipt

verify_branch_freeze(freeze_receipt, incident.branch) verify_checkpoint_chain(checkpoints, permit.archive_head) checkpoint = newest_eligible_known_good(checkpoints, incident)

if checkpoint exists: plan = RestorePlan(checkpoint, exact_constructor_path) residue = policy.restore_residue(frozen) else: floor = traverse_ordered_tree_to_atomic_floor(checkpoints.current_tree) witness = finite_diagonal_witness(frozen.evidence_rows, width=256) trace = bounded_collatz(derive_n0(frozen, witness), steps=10000, max_bits=4096) if trace.status != REACHED_ONE: return Hold(trace.status, no_mutation=true) seed = derive_nonzero_seed(frozen, witness, trace, bits=256) plan = SeedPublication(seed, floor, witness.digest, trace.digest) residue = policy.floor_residue(frozen, witness, trace)

if residue exists: rtsom_receipt = request_and_verify_rtsom_custody(residue) else: rtsom_receipt = NO_RESIDUE

delta_receipt = publish_once_and_verify_delta_consumption(plan) committed = commit_recovery_cas(tx, plan, rtsom_receipt, delta_receipt) recovery_receipt = emit_rover_receipt(committed) phi_event = emit_once_phi_completion_event(committed) return recovery_receipt

1. Normative Scope, Statement Classes, and Non-Goals 1.1 Module purpose Module 17 is a generic orchestration framework for conditional mathematical proof attempts. It does not supply a universal mathematical method. A conforming run is meaningful only after a domain adapter declares the formal language, semantics, axioms, premises, target statement, state representation, transition rules, monitor, anomaly predicates, intervention proof obligations, termination rule, and trusted verification procedure.

CORE BOUNDARY M_map defines the frozen formal task. M_evo, M_mon, M_loc, and M_int produce trace evidence and candidate transformations. M_acc records local run events. M_ver alone determines whether the declared kernel accepts a proof object or counterexample. M_rep reports that result without strengthening it. Psi may archive the artifact; Module 18 may later inspect evidence but receives no execution authority from Module 17.

1.3 Normative non-goals      Module 17 does not infer theoremhood from a high similarity, coherence, confidence, invariant, or progress score.      Module 17 does not treat numerical simulation, finite case checking, model agreement, or a replayable trace as a general proof unless the formal target explicitly reduces to those finite checks.      Module 17 does not import archive material as a premise merely because it is semantically similar or previously accepted by SpiralCore.      Module 17 does not let an external solver, language model, numerical package, or heuristic certify its own output without an independently declared checker.      Module 17 does not mutate the persistent Phi state, commit a .frac object, invoke RMX, execute FBS, take RTSOM custody, or compile a build directive.      The project name Millennium Architecture is historical. It is not an assertion that a Millennium Prize Problem has been solved or recognized by the mathematical community.

2.1 Trust boundary The trusted computing base is explicitly declared per run. At minimum it includes the canonical serializer, digest implementation, task parser, proof-object checker, exact arithmetic or interval checker, and result mapper. The generator, heuristic search, numerical simulator, archive retriever, and language model are outside the trusted kernel unless a separate proof establishes otherwise.

TRUSTED-KERNEL RULE A certificate may be tamper-evident and perfectly replayable while the mathematical conclusion is still invalid. CONDITIONAL_PROVED or CONDITIONAL_REFUTED requires independent kernel acceptance. Hashes bind evidence; they do not prove the evidence is correct.

2.2 Required handoff chain 1. The requester submits ProblemSpec and HypothesisSpec plus a registered domain profile. 2. M_map freezes the formal task and premise registry into RunManifest. 3. The sandbox executes the bounded pipeline and appends complete StepRecords. 4. M_ver checks the final proof object, counterexample, transition ledger, monitor bounds, and all intervention obligations. 5. M_rep emits one terminal result and CertificateBundle preserving the verifier status exactly. 6. Under archive policy, Module 17 submits an ArtifactArchiveRequest to Psi and waits for a matching receipt. 7. After durable archive acceptance, Module 17 may emit one Module17CompletionEventReceipt for Module 12 EVENT_APPEND. 8. A downstream build directive, if any, is separately submitted to Module 18 and carries no inherited execution permission.

2.3 Prohibited cross-module mutation       No direct .frac addressing, Cantor-IP allocation, archive-head update, RMX synthesis, or Psi commit.       No direct Phi or global DeltaPhi update. M_acc is a run-local audit counter only.       No direct FBS, Cantor diagonalization, Collatz folding, reseeding, or RTSOM mutation.       No direct system modification, microcode registration, configuration write, or build-directive execution.

3.2 Frozen run manifest Before M_map begins, the coordinator freezes every item that can affect semantics or replay: task bytes, hypothesis bytes, adapter ID/version/digest, axiom set, premise set, theorem target, arithmetic backend, kernel ID/version/digest, resource limits, deterministic seed, archive-context digest, policy epoch, and output schema. Wall-clock time, process ID, host path, thread scheduling, and UI state are never semantic inputs.

3.3 Step atomicity 1. Read x_t and the prior ledger head without mutation. 2. Compute M_evo, M_mon, M_loc, and optional M_int outputs. 3. Verify schema, exact arithmetic evidence, intervention obligations, and output digest. 4. Construct one canonical StepRecord bound to the prior ledger head. 5. Append with compare-and-swap; publish x_{t+1} only after durable append succeeds. 6. On crash, either the step record and state are both visible or neither is visible.

4.1 Canonical serialization       All maps use lexicographically sorted UTF-8 keys; arrays preserve declared order; sets use an explicitly declared canonical sort.       Integers and rationals use canonical sign, numerator, and positive denominator encodings. Equivalent fractions are reduced before hashing.       Floating-point values cannot carry proof authority. Diagnostic floats use a declared finite-number profile and remain outside the proof kernel.       Every record includes schema version, producer ID/version, policy epoch, parent digest, object digest, and complete dependency digests.       The final certificate is identified by SHA-256 over canonical content. Optional signatures authenticate an issuer but do not replace mathematical checking.

4.2 Digest chain h_0 = SHA256(canonical(RunManifest)) h_{t+1} = SHA256(h_t || canonical(StepRecord_t)) certificate_digest = SHA256(h_T || canonical(VerificationRecord) || canonical(Report)) A missing, reordered, duplicated, or modified step changes the final digest. Digest continuity proves evidence integrity relative to the hash assumption; it does not prove the mathematical inference.

5. Formal Task, Domain Adapter, and Trusted Kernel 5.1 Formal task T = (L, Sem, A, H, G, X, O, K) L is the formal language; Sem is its semantics; A is the axiom set; H is the explicit premise registry; G is the target proposition or decision predicate; X is the state space; O is the complete proof-obligation set; and K is the declared verification kernel. A task is invalid when any of these components is absent, ambiguous, versionless, or internally inconsistent.

5.2 Premise registry and archive isolation Archive retrieval may suggest definitions, lemmas, examples, or prior certificates. It cannot silently become an assumption. Every archive-derived item used by the proof must become a PremiseRecord with exact source digest, formal statement, trust class, dependency closure, and checker status. Unverified archive material may guide search but cannot be consumed by M_ver as a proved premise.

5.3 Domain adapter contract Submodule          Normative contract

M_map              Parse and type-check P/H; build FormalTask and x_0; enumerate initial obligations

M_evo              Deterministic transition or search proposal; may be heuristic but must expose full evidence

M_mon              Return exact/inclusion-certified values and propagation metadata

M_loc              Return deterministic anomaly candidates; cannot edit state

M_int              Return a candidate transformation and proof obligations; cannot approve them

M_acc              Record local events, counts, and resource deltas; no persistent Phi mutation

Check task well-formedness, premises, transitions, obligations, proof object, counterexample, and conclusion M_ver mapping

M_rep              Render the verified result without altering its class or strength

5.4 Trusted kernel levels Level                         Requirement                                                         Meaning

TRACE_REPLAYED                All recorded transitions replay under the frozen adapter            Execution integrity only

OBLIGATIONS_CHECKED           Every required local/global obligation is accepted                  Certified transformation chain

PROOF_OBJECT_ACCEPTED         Minimal checker accepts proof object for G under A and H            CONDITIONAL_PROVED eligible

Level                     Requirement                                               Meaning

COUNTEREXAMPLE_ACCEPT Checker accepts witness in domain and verifies not-G      CONDITIONAL_REFUTED eligible ED

GENERATOR/CHECKER SEPARATION The same code may propose and check an object only when the checker is separately instantiated from immutable bytes and its trusted boundary is declared. A solver saying “SAT,” a model saying “proved,” or an intervention reporting “invariants preserved” is not a kernel result.

6. Eight-Stage Pipeline Mechanics 6.1 M_map - deterministic formalization (T, x_0, O_0) = M_map(P, H, adapter, premise_registry)      Rejects ambiguous symbol binding, undeclared quantifiers, incompatible domains, circular premises, and missing target semantics.      Produces one canonical formalization digest. A changed formalization is a new task, not a continuation of the old run.      Records any human-authored or machine-generated translation assumptions explicitly.

6.2 M_evo - bounded deterministic evolution x_{t+1}^{evo} = M_evo(x_t, T, seed, t) M_evo may implement exact deduction, state exploration, numerical approximation, graph rewriting, symbolic algebra, or a problem-specific flow. It must be deterministic under the frozen manifest or record all controlled nondeterminism as explicit input. Its output is a candidate state, not a proof.

6.3 M_mon - exact or inclusion-certified monitor I_t = [l_t, u_t] subset Q, V_S(x_t) in I_t M_mon reports the quantity definition, interval or exact rational value, checker, and dependency evidence. A bare epsilon claim is insufficient. The checker must be able to verify that the true target quantity is contained in the declared interval under the formal model.

6.4 M_loc - anomaly localization A_t = sort(M_loc(neighborhood(x_{t+1}^{evo}), T)) Anomalies are typed predicates such as violated preconditions, nonregular boundaries, rank loss, cycle recurrence, domain escape, or unsatisfied local constraints. Results use stable priority and identifier ordering. M_loc is read-only.

6.5 M_int - certified intervention proposal (x_{t+1}, pi_t^{int}, O_t^{int}) = M_int(x_{t+1}^{evo}, A_t, T) The intervention does not “preserve invariants” by declaration. It emits a transformed state plus exact proof obligations for domain membership, boundary compatibility, invariant transfer, dependency retention, and postconditions. M_ver or a registered local checker must discharge them before the step commits.

6.6 M_acc - local event accounting e_t in {0,1}, N_event(T) = sum_{t=0}^{T-1} e_t M_acc records whether a registered critical transformation occurred and accumulates a run-local event count. The legacy name DeltaPhi_local may be retained as a compatibility field, but it is not the persistent Module 12 DeltaPhi, a topological winding number, proof of work, or evidence of theorem depth.

Page 8

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 17 / Conditional Proof Pipeline

6.7 M_ver - independent verification 1. Validate FormalTask, premise closure, adapter/kernel identities, and manifest digest. 2. Validate every StepRecord and ledger link, or validate a proof object that safely abstracts the trace under the declared kernel. 3. Check every mandatory monitor inclusion and intervention obligation. 4. Check proof object or counterexample against the exact target G. 5. Map the kernel result to one terminal conclusion class using a fixed table.

6.8 M_rep - status-preserving report M_rep may improve readability but must not strengthen the result. “Inconclusive” cannot become “likely proved”; a finite test cannot become a theorem; a theorem under additional premises cannot be reported without those premises. The report embeds the exact formalization, assumptions, kernel, result, and limitations.

7. Proof Semantics, Conclusion Classes, and Verification Gate 7.1 Certificate classes Class                              Meaning

PROOF_CERTIFICATE                  Kernel-accepted proof object for G under exact A and H

COUNTEREXAMPLE_CERTIFICATE         Kernel-accepted witness establishing not-G in the declared domain

TRACE_CERTIFICATE                  Replayable execution trace without a theorem-level proof object

BOUND_CERTIFICATE                  Finite verified bounds or finite-case result only

INCONCLUSIVE_CERTIFICATE           Run ended without discharging all required obligations

INVALID_CERTIFICATE                Malformed, inconsistent, incomplete, or checker-rejected artifact

7.2 Terminal mathematical conclusions Conclusion                          Exact meaning

CONDITIONAL_PROVED                  K accepts proof object pi: A,H |- G; all mandatory dependencies and obligations verified

CONDITIONAL_REFUTED                 K accepts witness w: w in Domain and not G(w)

FINITE_DOMAIN_ESTABLISHED           Target is explicitly finite and every required case is checked

BOUND_ESTABLISHED                   A declared bound is verified without claiming the full target theorem

INCONCLUSIVE_MAX_STEPS              The bounded search ended; no proof or refutation follows

INCONCLUSIVE_UNDISCHARGED           One or more required obligations remain unresolved

INVALID_FORMALIZATION               Task, semantics, premises, or target are invalid or ambiguous

INVALID_PROOF_OBJECT                Kernel rejects the proposed proof or counterexample

7.3 Authoritative gate CONDITIONAL_PROVED iff kernel_accepts(pi, A, H, G) and unresolved_required = 0 CONDITIONAL_REFUTED iff kernel_accepts_counterexample(w, Domain, G) No averaged score can satisfy this gate. The source thresholds are retained only as legacy progress diagnostics:

Page 9

SPIRALCORE v14.1 - Module 17 / Conditional Proof Pipeline

Xi_progress = N_passed / N_required Omega_unresolved = N_unresolved / N_required For N_required=0, both metrics are NOT_READY. The legacy display condition Xi_progress >= 0.85 and Omega_unresolved <= 0.15 may be shown as “progress gate passed,” but it never authorizes proof status. A conforming proof requires every mandatory obligation to pass and the kernel to accept the final object.

NO PARTIAL PROOF BY SCORE A proof with 85% of obligations discharged is an incomplete proof. An unresolved-obligation ratio of 15% is not mathematically acceptable merely because it is small. These values are dashboard telemetry, not truth thresholds.

7.4 Required report language For a proved result, the report must use an equivalent of: “Under axiom set A, formalization F, explicit premise set H, and kernel K, proof object pi was accepted as establishing conclusion G.” For refutation, identify the exact witness. For every other outcome, state that the target was not proved or refuted by this run.

8. Exact Monitoring, Error Propagation, and Obligations 8.1 Exact and interval arithmetic      Exact integer, rational, algebraic, or symbolic arithmetic is preferred where feasible.      Interval arithmetic must use outward rounding or a checker-verifiable inclusion certificate.      A floating-point estimate with a self-reported epsilon is diagnostic until independently bounded.      Every comparison near a threshold uses interval logic: PASS only when the entire interval satisfies the predicate; FAIL when the entire interval violates it; otherwise UNRESOLVED.

8.2 Error propagation The source cumulative sum E_T = sum epsilon_t is not generally a valid global error bound because a transition may amplify earlier error. A conforming adapter declares a propagation rule. The reference Lipschitz profile uses: E_0 = 0 E_{t+1} <= L_t E_t + epsilon_{t+1}, L_t in Q_{>=0} Each L_t must be exact or certified. When the adapter cannot supply a valid propagation rule, accumulated numerical error remains UNKNOWN and cannot support a proof claim that depends on it.

8.3 Obligation classes Class                 Required verification

TASK                  Well-formed language, semantics, axioms, premises, target, and domain

TRANSITION            M_evo output follows the declared relation or is correctly labeled as a search proposal

MONITOR               Value inclusion, bound propagation, and threshold classification

ANOMALY               M_loc predicate and location are valid

INTERVENTION          Preconditions, boundary match, invariant transfer, postconditions, and lineage

TERMINATION           Termination reason and final-state relationship are valid

PROOF                 Proof object establishes G from A and H

COUNTEREXAMPLE        Witness lies in domain and falsifies G

9. Certified Intervention and Local Event Ledger 9.1 Intervention transaction 1. Bind the anomaly, pre-state, adapter, and parameter set. 2. Generate a candidate transformed state without overwriting the pre-state. 3. Emit exact proof obligations and a dependency-complete InterventionCertificate proposal. 4. Have the independent checker verify every mandatory obligation. 5. Append the accepted intervention and new state atomically, or append a rejected proposal while retaining x_t.

9.2 Required intervention evidence Evidence                        Requirement

Precondition                    The anomaly and intervention domain are satisfied

Boundary compatibility          Removed and inserted structures match under the declared boundary relation

Invariant transfer              Every claimed invariant has a proof or checker result

Dependency preservation         No premise, variable, branch, or constraint is silently discarded

Postcondition                   The transformed state belongs to X and satisfies the next-stage contract

Lineage                         Pre-state, anomaly, parameters, transformed state, and obligations are digest-bound

9.3 Local event count event_count_T = sum e_t, e_t = 1 only for a registered committed event The counter supports audit and workload metrics. It is not an unforgeable certificate, physical winding number, semantic holonomy, proof depth, or theorem-quality score. Duplicate retries and rejected interventions do not increment it.

10. Certificate, Reporting, Psi Archive, and Module 18 Boundary 10.1 Certificate minimum content      Canonical ProblemSpec, HypothesisSpec, FormalTask, axiom set, premise registry, and formalization digest.

      RunManifest with adapter, kernel, arithmetic backend, resource limits, deterministic inputs, and archive-context digest.       Complete step ledger or immutable content-addressed references sufficient for independent verification.       All monitor bounds, anomaly evidence, intervention proposals/certificates, and obligation statuses.       Proof object, counterexample, finite-case manifest, or explicit absence thereof.       VerificationRecord with kernel result, failed/unresolved obligations, checker digest, and replay digest.       Status-preserving human-readable report and exact conclusion class.       Certificate digest and optional external signature/countersignature metadata.

10.2 Tamper evidence versus authenticity The digest chain detects modification relative to SHA-256. A signature authenticates the signer relative to its key- management system. Neither mechanism proves the theorem. The verifier must still check the mathematical object and its assumptions. “Unforgeable certificate” is replaced by “tamper-evident certificate with optional authenticated signature.”

10.3 Psi archival 1. Module 17 emits ArtifactArchiveRequest only after M_rep has finalized the certificate. 2. Psi validates the request, performs its own address/RMX/commit workflow, and returns PsiArchiveReceipt. 3. Module 17 verifies exact certificate digest, archive head, commit sequence, and receipt authenticity. 4. Archive failure or contention does not change the mathematical result; it changes archive status only.

10.4 Module 12 event After durable Psi acceptance, Module 17 may emit one Module17CompletionEventReceipt. Module 12 decides whether and how to record it. The proof run never writes persistent Phi state directly, and its local event count is not copied into global DeltaPhi.

10.5 Module 18 boundary A proof certificate may support a later build directive, but it cannot authorize execution or self-modification. Module 17 may emit BuildDirectiveEvidencePacket containing exact certificate and claim digests. Module 18 independently validates directive syntax, registry binding, stack and policy constraints, and execution authority. A mathematically valid theorem does not automatically imply a safe or authorized software change.

11. Sandbox, Security, Resource Bounds, and Replay 11.1 Sandbox requirements       No network access unless the run manifest explicitly declares a read-only deterministic content source whose bytes are frozen before execution.       No write access outside the run workspace; no shell, device, credential, or host-control capability for domain adapters.       CPU, memory, state size, certificate size, recursion depth, intervention count, solver calls, and logical-step budgets are hard limits.       Randomness uses an explicit deterministic seed and algorithm. Uncontrolled concurrency is prohibited in proof- authoritative paths.       External solvers are version-locked and treated as untrusted generators unless their proof objects are independently checked.

11.2 Threat model Threat                       Control

Premise injection            Only registered, typed, dependency-complete premises may enter M_ver

Proof-by-hash                Digests bind artifacts but never satisfy proof obligations

12.3 Catastrophic incidents 1. Verified deterministic replay divergence after the same manifest and environment digest. 2. Conflicting persisted kernel results for the same proof object, task, kernel version, and dependency closure. 3. A committed step-ledger split, double finalization, or contradictory terminal certificate for one run ID. 4. Sandbox escape, unauthorized host mutation, or evidence that the run modified external state outside its declared capabilities. 5. Durable certificate/object loss after an acknowledged Psi receipt or an accepted certificate digest changing on read- back. 6. A forged or multiply consumed recovery/archive token that was accepted as valid. Module 17 freezes the run, emits CatastrophicIncidentPacket to ROVER, and stops. It does not execute FBS, Cantor processing, Collatz processing, reseeding, or RTSOM custody.

14.2 Property and metamorphic tests    Canonical-renaming property: alpha-equivalent bound-variable renaming produces the same normalized formal task when the language profile declares alpha equivalence.    Premise monotonicity is never assumed globally; adding a premise creates a new task and result even when the target remains provable.    Trace integrity: any permutation, omission, duplication, or modification of StepRecords changes the certificate digest or fails sequence checks.    Checker independence: replacing M_rep wording cannot change the kernel result or proof-object digest.    Score irrelevance: arbitrary Xi_progress and Omega_unresolved values cannot override obligation or kernel results.    Archive isolation: changing unused archive context changes context digest but not formal-task semantics or verifier result.

14.3 Fuzz, concurrency, crash, and stress requirements    Fuzz Unicode normalization, deeply nested syntax, huge integers/rationals, malformed proof objects, cyclic dependencies, NaN/Inf diagnostics, duplicate IDs, and certificate truncation.    Run concurrent archive submissions and verify Psi receipts cannot be cross-bound between certificates.    Crash at every step-transaction boundary, verification boundary, report write, archive request, and receipt reconciliation point.    Stress at least 100,000 bounded synthetic runs across proved, refuted, inconclusive, held, and faulted fixtures; reconcile every dashboard equation.    Differentially test independent checker implementations where two trusted kernels are available; disagreement is a fault or incident, never a majority vote.

15. Reference Pseudocode and ASCII System Flow 15.1 Proof-attempt pseudocode function run_millennium(request, config): validate_config_and_registry(config) manifest = freeze_run_manifest(request, config) task, x, obligations = M_map(manifest) ledger_head = sha256(canonical(manifest)) local_event_count = 0

for t in range(manifest.max_steps): if M_ver.termination_condition(task, x, t): break

x_evo = M_evo(task, x, t, manifest.seed) monitor = M_mon(task, x_evo, t) verify_monitor_evidence(monitor)

anomalies = stable_sort(M_loc(task, x_evo, t)) intervention = NONE x_next = x_evo

if anomalies is not empty: proposal = M_int(task, x_evo, anomalies, t) result = check_intervention_obligations(task, proposal) intervention = record(proposal, result) if result.all_mandatory_pass: x_next = proposal.output_state if proposal.registered_event: local_event_count += 1

step = build_step_record(t, x, x_evo, monitor, anomalies, intervention, x_next, ledger_head) append_step_and_state_cas(step, x_next) ledger_head = step.digest x = x_next

freeze_sandbox() proof_or_witness = adapter.final_object(task, x, ledger_head) verification = M_ver.verify(task, ledger_head, proof_or_witness) conclusion = map_kernel_result_exactly(verification) report = M_rep.render(task, conclusion, verification, local_event_count) certificate = build_certificate(manifest, ledger_head, proof_or_witness, verification, report) return typed_terminal_result(conclusion, certificate)

1. Normative Scope, Statement Classes, and Non-Goals 1.1 Module purpose Module 18 is the terminal compiler and change-plan builder for SpiralCore AI Build Directives. It transforms a typed, authenticated proposal into a canonical intermediate representation, resolves every operation against a signed registry snapshot, verifies types, capabilities, effects, preconditions, resource bounds, rollback requirements, and evidence bindings, and emits a non-executable package for independent authorization and target-owned execution.

Core rule The compiler may describe a change. Only the independent Change Control Authority may authorize it, and only the declared target owner may execute it.

REQUIREMENT         Mandatory implementation behavior.                         Canonical parse and exact registry lookup

INVARIANT           Condition that must hold for every conforming run.         No execution without an external permit

POLICY              Versioned deployment choice.                               Stack cap, fuel cap, allowed opcode set

SURROGATE           Computational quantity using project terminology.          Instruction Coherence telemetry

HYPOTHESIS          Interpretation requiring separate evidence.                Claims about cognition or systemic identity

NON-GOAL            Behavior intentionally excluded.                           Direct root-state self-modification

1.3 Normative non-goals       No free-form text is executed as code.       No SHA-256 digest is treated as a semantic embedding, opcode selector, or collision-free identifier.       No cosine similarity score grants capability, privilege, or root-state write authority.       No directive may alter the active compiler, active registry, policy epoch, target state, archive, network, Phi state, or recovery seed during compilation.       No stack-depth check alone is claimed to prove termination.       No rejected directive is labeled malicious, hallucinatory, or unsafe merely because it fails compilation.       No ordinary parse, type, policy, stack, fuel, or sandbox failure triggers catastrophic recovery.

2.1 Trust boundary Module 18 treats the proposer, free-form source text, Module 17 evidence, external generators, target adapters, and sandbox runtime as untrusted until their outputs satisfy exact typed checks. The trusted base is limited to the frozen compiler build, canonical serializer, parser, registry-verification logic, policy evaluator, cryptographic primitive implementation, and independent package verifier named by the run manifest.

2.2 Required handoff chain 1. Authenticated DirectiveEnvelope enters Module 18. Remote envelopes require a Guardian receipt. 2. Module 18 freezes the directive, registry, policy, target snapshot, evidence references, and resource limits. 3. Module 18 parses, resolves, statically validates, sandbox-executes where required, and emits DirectivePlanPacket. 4. The independent package verifier replays and verifies the package. 5. Module 18 emits ChangeAuthorizationRequest; the Change Control Authority issues or denies ChangeExecutionPermit. 6. The declared target owner consumes the single-use permit, prepares and commits through compare-and-swap, verifies postconditions, and returns ExecutionReceipt or RollbackReceipt. 7. Psi may archive the plan and receipts. Module 12 may consume one committed-change event receipt.

4.1 Canonical serialization       UTF-8 text is normalized to Unicode NFC before parsing; identifiers use registered ASCII profiles unless a schema explicitly permits otherwise.       Maps use lexicographically sorted keys; arrays preserve declared order; integers use minimal decimal encoding; binary data uses lowercase hexadecimal.       Floating-point values are prohibited in authoritative directive semantics unless a registered schema defines exact rational or bit-level encoding.       Unknown fields, duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, ambiguous numeric forms, and unregistered extensions are rejected.       Canonical bytes include all version, target, policy, registry, capability, effect, evidence, and rollback fields.

h_dir = SHA256(canonical(DirectiveEnvelope)) h_plan = SHA256(canonical(DirectivePlanPacket without h_plan)) SHA-256 is used as a collision-resistant content address and integrity binding. It is not claimed to be collision-free, semantic, self-authenticating, or sufficient for authorization.

4.2 Signatures and replay Signatures authenticate an issuer relative to the configured trust store. A signature does not prove that the directive is correct or permitted. Nonce, issuer sequence, expiry, parent digest, and package-consumption records prevent replay. Repeated submission of identical canonical bytes is idempotent and returns the prior compile result.

5. Directive Language, Registry, Capability, and Effect Model 5.1 Directive language The reference profile accepts a small declarative DSL or its equivalent typed AST. It does not accept shell commands, Python source, native code, arbitrary bytecode, SQL strings, network payloads, or templated text for direct execution. Free-form language may be used only by an untrusted proposer that outputs a DirectiveAST for exact compiler validation.

Reference opcode          Meaning                                                                      Required capability

SET_CONFIG                Set a registered configuration field                                         CONFIG_WRITE

REGISTER_ARTIFACT         Register an immutable, verified artifact for later target-owned activation   ARTIFACT_REGISTER

ENABLE_FEATURE            Enable a pre-registered feature flag                                         FEATURE_CONTROL

DISABLE_FEATURE           Disable a pre-registered feature flag                                        FEATURE_CONTROL

UPDATE_POLICY_REF         Point a target to an already-published signed policy version                 POLICY_REF_WRITE

MIGRATE_SCHEMA            Apply a registered, reversible schema migration                              SCHEMA_MIGRATE

NO_OP                     Produce a receipt without target mutation                                    NONE

5.2 Exact registry lookup The directive carries opcode_id and opcode_version. Module 18 performs exact lookup in the frozen RegistrySnapshot. A hash is never converted into an opcode and cyclic modulo mapping is prohibited in authoritative compilation. opcode = RegistrySnapshot[(opcode_id, opcode_version)]

5.3 Capability model Every opcode declares a minimal capability set. The directive requests capabilities, policy limits the request, and the external permit grants an exact subset. Module 18 can prove that a requested package is internally capability- consistent, but it cannot grant the capabilities. C_required = union_j C(op_j) C_required ⊆ C_requested ⊆ C_policy_ceiling C_granted = C_required Required for execution; evaluated by the external Change Control Authority.

5.4 Effect model Each opcode declares explicit read and write effects. Hidden effects are prohibited. A package whose inferred effects differ from declared effects is rejected. The effect manifest distinguishes target state, archive state, registry state, routing state, network egress, credential access, process creation, and external I/O. E_inferred = union_j E(op_j, operands_j)

E_inferred = E_declared

Root and self-hosting rule The active compiler, active registry, root trust store, Change Control Authority, and permit-verification code cannot be modified through an ordinary directive. A separately registered bootstrap profile requires an offline signed artifact, two independent verifiers, a restart-bound epoch swap, a recovery image, and external operator approval.

6. Compiler Pipeline Mechanics 6.1 Stage A - ingest and freeze Validate envelope signature, issuer, nonce, expiry, profile, target, source kind, and maximum byte length. Freeze all dependencies in CompilationManifest. No parsing occurs before the manifest is durable.

6.2 Stage B - canonicalize and parse Canonicalize source bytes under the declared grammar, parse into DirectiveAST, reject ambiguity, duplicate keys, unknown syntax, undeclared extensions, and host-language escapes. Parsing must be total over accepted input and bounded by AST node and depth limits.

6.3 Stage C - registry and schema resolution Resolve every opcode, operand schema, target adapter, capability, effect class, and rollback schema against exact versioned identifiers. Missing or revoked registry entries produce typed rejection. Registry order cannot affect resolution.

6.4 Stage D - type, precondition, and effect checking Type-check all operands; verify target-state version and preconditions against the frozen snapshot; infer effects; ensure the effect manifest is complete; reject privilege amplification, undeclared writes, wildcard targets, and ambiguous ownership.

6.5 Stage E - dependency and termination analysis Build the directive call/dependency graph, reject cycles unless the relevant opcode supplies a registered well-founded ranking function, compute stack depth, expansion nodes, instruction count, cost, and fuel, and prove all values remain within policy.

6.6 Stage F - rollback construction Every mutating opcode must produce a target-owned rollback operation or a registered proof that the operation is immutable and safely additive. Rollback is checked against the same registry, target, capabilities, and effects as the forward plan.

6.7 Stage G - sandbox dry run Where policy requires, execute the target adapter in a deterministic sandbox against a copy of the frozen target snapshot. Compare declared and observed effects, verify postconditions, record resource use, and rerun to detect nondeterminism. The sandbox has no authority to commit.

6.8 Stage H - package and independent verify Construct DirectivePlanPacket, compute h_plan, and invoke the independent package verifier. VERIFY_PACKAGE must reproduce the AST digest, resolved registry entries, static results, sandbox evidence, operation order, effect manifest, rollback plan, and h_plan from immutable inputs.

7. Validation Gate and Instruction Coherence Telemetry 7.1 Mandatory hard obligations Flag                    Mandatory obligation

b_parse                 Canonical parse and grammar acceptance

b_schema                Every operand and output satisfies its exact schema

b_registry              Every opcode, target adapter, and extension resolves to a valid signed registry record

b_type                  Static type checking passes

b_cap                   Required capabilities fit the requested set and policy ceiling

b_effect                Declared and inferred effects match exactly

b_pre                   All target preconditions hold on the frozen snapshot

b_resource              Depth, nodes, fuel, bytes, and cost are within limits

b_determinism           Compilation and required sandbox runs are deterministic

b_rollback              Rollback or immutable-additive exception is valid

b_evidence              Required Module 17 or external evidence is present and claim-bound

b_verify                Independent package verifier accepts

PLAN_READY = AND(b_parse, b_schema, b_registry, b_type, b_cap, b_effect, b_pre, b_resource, b_determinism, b_rollback, b_evidence, b_verify) A single false mandatory flag prevents PLAN_READY. No average, threshold, signature, proof certificate, or operator preference may override a hard failure.

7.2 Formalized Instruction Coherence telemetry The project name Φ_ins is retained as a diagnostic obligation-coverage score, not as an authorization metric. Let w_j > 0 be versioned diagnostic weights and b_j in {0,1} be the mandatory flags excluding b_verify during pre-verification telemetry. Φ_ins = (sum_j w_j b_j) / (sum_j w_j) 0 ≤ Φ_ins ≤ 1 The source INSTRUCTION_FLOOR = 0.80 is retained only as migration telemetry. A package with Φ_ins = 0.92 and one failed hard check is still rejected. A plan-ready reference package has Φ_ins = 1.00 before external authorization.

7.3 Legacy hash-similarity profile The original cosine similarity between a digest-derived vector and a registry vector is not semantic validation. Implementations may reproduce it only under LEGACY_HASH_SIMILARITY_V0 for migration dashboards. It must be labeled non-authoritative, must not select an opcode, and must not influence PLAN_READY, authorization, execution, rollback, FBS, or archive status.

8.1 Depth does not prove termination A maximum stack depth prevents unbounded nesting but does not prevent a loop at one level. The reference profile additionally requires a finite operation list, bounded expansion, a decreasing fuel counter, and an acyclic dependency graph unless a registered well-founded recursion measure is supplied. fuel_(k+1) = fuel_k - cost(op_k),      cost(op_k) ∈ N_{>0} fuel_k ≥ 0 for every executed compiler/sandbox step

8.2 Dependency graph The compiler constructs a directed graph over operations, artifacts, schemas, evidence, and target prerequisites. Stable topological ordering uses lexicographic identifier tie-breaking. Unregistered cycles are rejected with the full cycle witness.

8.3 Resource outcomes Exceeding a declared limit produces HELD_RESOURCE_LIMIT or REJECTED_LIMIT according to policy. It does not imply maliciousness and does not invoke FBS. Evidence is retained so the proposer may submit a smaller or differently scoped directive.

Sandbox, Static Analysis, Dry Run, and Deterministic Replay 9.1 Static analysis      No undeclared file, registry, archive, route, network, process, credential, device, or privilege effects.      No dynamic code loading, reflection, eval, shell expansion, templated execution, or host-language escape.      No path traversal, wildcard target, implicit default target, or ambient authority.      No target-owner mismatch or cross-module write outside the declared adapter.      No use of revoked opcode, schema, issuer, artifact, registry, or policy version.      No unbounded loop, unbounded allocation, uncontrolled concurrency, wall-clock dependency, or unseeded randomness.

9.2 Sandbox requirements      Read-only frozen target copy; no production credentials, sockets, devices, or host namespace writes.      Deterministic virtual clock, locale, filesystem order, environment, random seed, and concurrency schedule.      Resource limits enforced outside the adapter process.      Observed read/write/effect trace compared exactly against EffectManifest.      Postconditions checked by a verifier distinct from the adapter that proposed the result.      Sandbox timeout or crash yields a typed fault; it is not evidence of a system catastrophe.

10. Authorization, Target Execution, Rollback, and Receipts 10.1 EXEC_DIRECTIVE_BOUND semantics EXEC_DIRECTIVE_BOUND is retained as a legacy-visible label for PLAN_READY plus independent package verification. It means the directive package is complete and bound to exact evidence, registry, policy, target, effects, and rollback data. It does not grant execution authority and does not permit a kernel write or privilege escalation.

10.2 External authorization    Permit ID, issuer, signature, issued-at and expiry cycle.    Exact package digest and target-state snapshot digest.    Exact granted capability and effect sets; no wildcard authority.    Target owner and target adapter version.    Single-use consumption token and expected state version.    Review class, required countersignatures, and rollback requirement.

10.3 Target-owned two-phase execution 1. Target owner verifies permit, package, policy, registry, target snapshot, and unconsumed token. 2. PREPARE: target creates an isolated prepared state and validates forward preconditions. 3. COMMIT: target uses compare-and-swap from expected state version to prepared state. 4. READ-BACK: independent target verifier recomputes state digest and postconditions. 5. RECEIPT: target emits ExecutionReceipt and atomically consumes the permit. 6. ROLLBACK: on postcondition failure, the target executes the registered inverse and emits RollbackReceipt; Module 18 does not perform it.

10.4 Time-of-check/time-of-use protection The permit is bound to the exact target-state digest and expected version. Any intervening state change invalidates the prepare or commit and requires recompilation or reauthorization. A stale package cannot be silently rebased.

11. Archive, Event, Recovery, and Cross-Module Boundaries 11.1 Module 17 evidence boundary A Module 17 proof certificate may justify a precondition or artifact claim only when the exact claim and certificate digests are imported into BuildDirectiveEvidencePacket. The certificate does not authorize execution. Module 18 independently validates syntax, registry binding, capabilities, effects, policy, target ownership, resources, rollback, and package verification.

11.2 Psi and RMX boundary Module 18 emits ArtifactArchiveRequest for the directive package, verifier record, authorization decision, and execution/rollback receipts. Psi owns address allocation, RMX resolution, archive commit, and archive receipts. Archive failure does not change compile, authorization, or target-execution status.

11.3 Module 12 event boundary Compilation, verification, authorization, and rejected directives do not increment persistent Phi. After a target owner has durably committed and Psi has accepted the corresponding receipt, the target may emit one Module18ChangeCompletionEventReceipt. Module 12 decides whether and how to record it exactly once.

11.4 Guardian and network boundary Remote directive ingress and remote artifact egress require Guardian authorization. QGM/GlyphNet and the host network stack transport opaque, authenticated packets only. Module 18 does not choose routes, endpoints, IPv4 addresses, or sockets.

11.5 ROVER, FBS, and RTSOM boundary Stack overflow, parse rejection, type failure, policy denial, sandbox crash, resource exhaustion, and target contention are ordinary outcomes. Module 18 may report a catastrophic incident only for persisted control-plane corruption such as conflicting signed registry roots or contradictory committed receipts. ROVER decides whether to issue an FBS activation permit; FBS executes recovery; RTSOM accepts only registered, receipted recovery residue.

12. Security Model and Registry Governance 12.1 Threat model Threat                        Control

Prompt/directive injection    Only canonical DSL/AST enters the authoritative compiler; free-form source never executes

Hash-to-semantics confusion   Digest is identity only; exact opcode lookup is mandatory

Registry poisoning            Signed monotonic snapshots, publisher allow-list, revocation checks, offline validation, atomic epoch swap

Confused deputy               Capabilities and effects bound to target owner and external permit

Privilege escalation          No wildcard effects; exact C_required = C_granted at execution

TOCTOU                        Permit binds target state digest/version; target uses compare-and-swap

Replay                        Nonce, issuer sequence, expiry, parent digest, and single-use token ledger

Compiler self-modification    Ordinary directives cannot target active compiler/registry/trust roots

Dependency substitution       Every artifact, schema, evidence packet, and adapter is digest-bound

Nondeterminism                Frozen environment and repeated sandbox/replay checks

Rollback gap                  Mutating operation requires registered inverse or immutable-additive proof

Receipt forgery               Signed target receipt plus package, permit, state, and sequence reconciliation

12.2 Registry publication 1. Validate candidate registry offline, including schemas, ownership, capabilities, effects, costs, pre/postconditions, and rollback definitions. 2. Assign a monotonic registry version and compute the canonical root digest. 3. Sign with an authorized Registry Authority key and publish revocation metadata. 4. Activate through an atomic epoch swap; in-flight compilations continue using their frozen snapshot. 5. Retain the prior registry and migration rules for deterministic replay and rollback.

12.3 Key and trust governance Module 18 assumes an external key-management and identity system. Key creation, rotation, revocation, threshold signatures, operator identity, and emergency trust-root recovery are outside Module 18. A cryptographic signature is accepted only after trust-chain, purpose, time, revocation, and algorithm-policy validation.

13. Outcomes, Invariants, Faults, and Catastrophic Incidents 13.1 Normative invariants Invariant           Requirement

M18-I01             Every compilation has one frozen CompilationManifest before parsing.

M18-I02             Identical canonical inputs and manifest produce identical compilation artifacts and outcome.

M18-I03             Free-form text is never executed directly.

M18-I04             Opcode resolution uses exact registered identifiers, never digest similarity or modulo mapping.

M18-I05             SHA-256 binds canonical bytes but never supplies semantic or authorization authority.

M18-I07             Declared and inferred effects are identical for PLAN_READY packages.

M18-I08             No average score overrides a failed mandatory obligation.

M18-I09             MAX_STACK_DEPTH = 8 is enforced and does not replace fuel/dependency termination checks.

M18-I10             Compilation and package verification do not mutate the target state.

M18-I11             Module 18 cannot issue its own ChangeExecutionPermit.

M18-I12             A permit is single-use and bound to exact package, target, state version, capabilities, effects, and expiry.

M18-I13             Only the target owner may prepare, commit, verify, or roll back target state.

M18-I14             The active compiler, registry, trust roots, and Change Control Authority are not ordinary directive targets.

M18-I15             Archive status is independent of compilation and execution status.

M18-I16             Persistent Phi changes only through a Module 12-owned, exactly-once event transaction after committed change.

M18-I17             Ordinary rejection, denial, limits, timeout, or stack overflow never triggers FBS.

M18-I18             Module 18 never mutates QGM/GlyphNet, network, Psi, RMX, RTSOM, or FBS state.

M18-I19             Rejected evidence and packages are retained or receipted according to policy; no silent deletion.

M18-I20             Every terminal outcome emits a canonical result record with a no-target-mutation assertion.

15.2 Property and metamorphic tests       Canonicalization idempotency: canonical(canonical(x)) = canonical(x).       Permutation of registry storage order does not change resolution or package digest.       Adding an unused registry entry does not change an existing package.       Narrowing policy capabilities cannot turn a rejected privilege request into an accepted one.       Adding a mandatory failed obligation cannot increase PLAN_READY or authorization eligibility.       Changing any target, effect, capability, evidence, rollback, policy, registry, or adapter field changes h_plan.       Compile-only and verify-package profiles agree on every canonical package field.       Repeated deterministic sandbox execution yields the same observed-effect and output digests.

15.3 Fuzz, concurrency, crash, and stress requirements       Fuzz parsers with malformed UTF-8, Unicode confusables, duplicate keys, deeply nested arrays, huge integers, invalid tags, and embedded NUL bytes.       Fuzz schemas, registry references, capability/effect combinations, dependency graphs, rollback definitions, signatures, and receipt bindings.

16. Reference Pseudocode and ASCII System Flow 16.1 Compile-only pseudocode function compile_directive(envelope, context): manifest = freeze_manifest( compiler=context.compiler, parser=context.parser, serializer=context.serializer, registry=context.registry_snapshot, policy=context.policy_snapshot, target=context.target_snapshot, evidence=context.evidence_snapshots, limits=context.resource_limits, sandbox=context.sandbox_image, verifier=context.package_verifier )

require verify_envelope_signature(envelope) require not_expired(envelope) require replay_guard_accepts(envelope.issuer, envelope.nonce)

canonical_bytes = canonicalize(envelope) h_dir = sha256(canonical_bytes) ast = parse_typed_directive(canonical_bytes, manifest.parser)

resolved = resolve_exact_registry_ids(ast, manifest.registry) require type_check(resolved) required_caps = infer_capabilities(resolved) inferred_effects = infer_effects(resolved, manifest.target) require required_caps <= envelope.requested_capabilities require envelope.requested_capabilities <= manifest.policy.capability_ceiling require inferred_effects == envelope.declared_effects require check_preconditions(resolved, manifest.target)

graph = build_dependency_graph(resolved) require bounded_and_terminating(graph, ast, manifest.limits) rollback = build_and_verify_rollback(resolved, manifest.registry)

static_record = make_static_analysis_record(...) sandbox_evidence = run_required_deterministic_sandbox( resolved, manifest.target, inferred_effects, manifest.sandbox )

plan = build_directive_plan( manifest, h_dir, ast, resolved, required_caps, inferred_effects, static_record, rollback, sandbox_evidence ) plan.h_plan = sha256(canonical(plan without h_plan))

verification = independent_verify(plan, manifest.package_verifier) require verification.accepted

return PLAN_READY(plan, verification, no_target_mutation=true)

17.4 Implementation checklist [ ] Implement the registered declarative DSL and reject all host-language execution paths. [ ] Freeze compiler, parser, serializer, registry, policy, target, evidence, limits, sandbox, and verifier before parsing. [ ] Use exact opcode/version lookup; never map hash bytes to semantic operations. [ ] Implement canonical serialization, h_dir, h_plan, signature validation, nonce/sequence replay protection, and single-use permit tracking. [ ] Enforce types, target ownership, capabilities, effects, preconditions, dependencies, resource bounds, deterministic behavior, and rollback. [ ] Keep Φ_ins and legacy hash similarity diagnostic only. [ ] Run required operations in an isolated deterministic sandbox and compare observed versus declared effects. [ ] Use an independent package verifier and an external Change Control Authority. [ ] Require target-owned prepare, compare-and-swap, read-back verification, receipts, and rollback. [ ] Keep Psi/RMX archive, Module 12 events, Guardian, QGM/GlyphNet, ROVER/FBS recovery, and RTSOM custody outside Module 18 ownership. [ ] Run all 60 conformance tests plus property, fuzz, concurrency, crash, and stress suites. [ ] Render, inspect, accessibility-audit, and independently verify the final DOCX/PDF artifacts.
